Function-identifier
notes: PARTIAL, not CONFORMS. The FUNCTION-keyword form is fully enforced: the lexer already gives the '(' after a function name to the argument list, and a ref-mod written there instead is rejected with COBOLNET1543 citing SR6 (the standard's own RANDOM trap). The KEYWORD-OMITTED form rejects the same shape through the ordinary unresolved-name path rather than the SR6 message, and RANDOM in particular cannot be written keyword-omitted at all because it lexes as a reserved word - fix-queue PB9 owns that.

Arithmetic expressions
notes: CONFORMS as of 2026-08-03 (fix-queue PB28, landed this session). Rule 6 has three parts. r6a (zero base requires exponent > 0) and r6c (negative base requires an integer exponent) are mandatory 'shall' requirements setting EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION, Fatal in Table 14. BEFORE the fix the STANDARD-DECIMAL arm enforced both (CobolDec.Pow) and EVERY NATIVE arm enforced neither, so the same program answered differently depending only on whether an ARITHMETIC clause was present: 0 ** 0 returned 1 (IEEE's convention, not COBOL's) and -2 ** 0.5 returned 0 (Math.Pow yields NaN and the quantizer made it zero), both with an ON SIZE ERROR phrase present and NOT taken. CheckPowRule6 now screens every native arm. MEASURED ACROSS EVERY REACHABLE COMBINATION, not sampled: native at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023, and ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL at 2023 - all five raise both legs and leave the receiver unmodified per SS14.7.5. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is loudly refused (COBOLNET0806), so that arm is unreachable rather than unverified. r6b ('if the evaluation yields both a positive and a negative real number, the value returned is the positive number') is a SELECTION rule, not a screen, and cannot arise here: both bodies (CobolIntrinsics.PowNativeInt / PowNativeReal and CobolDec.Pow) yield a single value. Checked in the same pass rather than left to be discovered as a fourth leg.

Re-verified by running src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe: an alphanumeric literal ("ABCDE"=5), a national literal (N"ABCD"=8), a BASED entry (`01 BE BASED. 05 BA PIC X(6).` = 6) and a data item of any class/category all answer. TWO admitted forms are REJECTED, both by falling into an arm of BindByteLengthFold that emits a BoundExprError -> NumericRenderer LoudValue -> a RUN-TIME NotImplementedCobolFeatureException after a ZERO-DIAGNOSTIC compile. (1) TYPE-NAME. `01 TN TYPEDEF. 05 TA PIC X(7).` + `DISPLAY FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(TN).` -> compiles clean, then throws "FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH argument (a numeric/figurative literal is not a valid argument, ISO 15.14.3)" (the `_ =>` fall-through, whose message also MISDIAGNOSES a legal argument as an illegal literal). Expected 7. A type-name IS legal: §15.14.3 r1 names it, §15.3 item 14 defines it ("A type-name shall be specified", cite.py OK), Table 21's BYTE-LENGTH row lists Type1, and §15.14.4 r2 a) presupposes it. (2) REFERENCE-MODIFIED DATA ITEM — MISSED BY THE FIRST PASS. `01 X PIC X(10) VALUE "ABCDEFGHIJ".` + `DISPLAY FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(X(1:3)).` -> compiles clean, then throws "FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH of a reference-modified argument (runtime length, 15.14.4)" (the `BoundFieldOperand { Place: RefModPlace }` arm). Expected 3. §8.4.3.3.4 GR5 (cite.py OK) "Reference modification creates a unique data item that is a subset of the data item referenced by identifier-1" and GR6 (cite.py OK) "The unique data item ... has the same class, category, and usage as that defined for identifier-1" — so a reference-modified operand IS 'a data item of any class or category' and r1 admits it; with a LITERAL length it is even foldable. This warning mechanism shall indicate violations of ...") requires the compile-time mechanism to flag exactly this. BYTE-LENGTH is deliberately ABSENT from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified and its doc-comment says so at line 125 ("BYTE-LENGTH is declared \"s\" while §15.14.3 admits an argument ...") — correct, because §15.14.3 admits any CLASS, so the PB1 class screen is the wrong mechanism; the literal/type-name/ref-mod restriction is a SHAPE rule. The prior pass verified only NON-EMPTY literals and so missed a SILENT wrong value on the ZERO-LENGTH LITERAL, which the fold's own `Math.Max(1, ...)` guarantees. Failing input, run verbatim: `IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. RVZL01. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 W PIC X(3). PROCEDURE DIVISION. DISPLAY "ZLA=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(""). DISPLAY "ZLN=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(N""). DISPLAY "LENZLA=" FUNCTION LENGTH(""). STOP RUN.` -> prints `ZLA=1`, `ZLN=2`, `LENZLA=1`. The spec answer is 0, 0 and 0: §8.3.3.1 (cite.py OK) "If the opening and closing delimiters are contiguous, the length of the literal is zero, and it is known as a zero-length literal"; §8.5.4 (cite.py OK) "A zero-length item is a data item or a literal whose minimum length is zero and whose length at runtime is zero", item 8 "A zero-length literal"; §15.14.4 r1 (cite.py OK) "The returned value is an integer that is the length of argument-1 in number of bytes" = 0. No diagnostic is issued. ROOT CAUSE is one expression in each literal arm of BindByteLengthFold: `Math.Max(1, s.Value.Length)` and `2 * Math.Max(1, s.Value.Length)` clamp a legal zero to one; the data-item arm carries the same clamp, `Math.Max(1, f.Place.Item.ByteWidth)`. SIBLING TO SWEEP: BindLengthFold in the same file has the identical clamp (LENGTH("") = 1, §15.50.4 r1 says 0). VERIFIED-CORRECT HALF (all run through the CLI): for a fixed-length data item or a non-empty literal the fold returns the right byte count against COBOL.NET's pinned implementor widths (§13.18.60.4 GR4/GR5/GR10 leave them implementor-defined; docs/CONFORMANCE.md rows 205/211 document them) — PIC X(5)=5, PIC N(4)=8, PIC 9(4)=4, PIC 9(4) COMP=2, PIC S9(5) COMP-3=3, BINARY-CHAR=1, INDEX=8, POINTER=8, group X(3)+N(2)=7, "ABCDE"=5, N"ABCD"=8. STILL-OPEN HALVES: a USAGE BIT item answers n instead of ceil(n/8) (RV-15.14.4-4) and a variable-length group answers a silently short constant (RV-15.14.4-6); a reference-modified argument and an ANY LENGTH item are staged loud (AR-15.14.3-1). The cited conformance-test was READ ON DISK at tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs line 928 and its AssertSpec helper (line 26) compiles under COBOL.NET at the named dialect and asserts a LITERAL expected string with NO oracle call — genuinely spec-derived, and it exercises r1 head-on (6 from §15.14.4 r1 vs 3 from §15.50.4 r2). It covers only the fixed-width half; the zero-length, BIT and variable-length legs are test-needed. Editions per the AR-15.14.3-1 derivation.

subject: BYTE-LENGTH function
notes: test-needed. VERDICT SURVIVES REVIEW, re-verified by running — the worst finding in this batch, a SILENT wrong value with no diagnostic and no loud stage. A variable-length group (§8.5.1.12.1, cite.py OK: 'a group item whose data description has at least one dynamic-length elementary item or dynamic-capacity table as a subordinate item') folds to a compile-time constant that omits exactly the variable part. §15.3 permits it as an argument ('A variable-length group shall be referenced as an argument to a function only when explicitly permitted in the function definition' — §15.14.4 r6/r7 explicitly permit it). Failing input, run verbatim: `IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. RVVLG01. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 VLG. 05 F1 PIC X(4). 05 DL PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH. 01 DCG. 05 F2 PIC X(2). 05 DT OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY IN CAP PIC X(3). PROCEDURE DIVISION. MOVE "HELLO" TO DL DISPLAY "LEN-DL=" FUNCTION LENGTH(DL). DISPLAY "BL-VLG=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(VLG). DISPLAY "CAP=" CAP. DISPLAY "BL-DCG=" FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(DCG). STOP RUN.` -> prints LEN-DL=5, BL-VLG=4, CAP=0000000000, BL-DCG=5. Spec: BYTE-LENGTH(VLG) = r6 a) 4 + r6 b) 5 = 9, COBOL.NET says 4 (DL contributes 0 because ElementaryImageWidth returns 0 for IsDynamicLength). BYTE-LENGTH(DCG) at capacity 0 = r6 a) 2 + r6 c) 0 = 2, COBOL.NET says 5 (ByteWidth multiplies the dynamic table by `c.Occurs ?? 1`, one phantom element). A SECOND run confirms the constant never tracks capacity: after `MOVE "AAA" TO DT(4)` the program prints CAP=0000000004 and BL-DCG=5, where r6 c) requires 2 + 4 x 3 = 14. ROOT CAUSE, one place: BindByteLengthFold's ONLY variable-length guard is `OdoModel.TableUnder(item) is { OccursSpec.Depending: not null }`, and OdoModel.TableUnder walks for OCCURS DEPENDING children ONLY (`c.OccursSpec is { DependingName: not null }`) — it sees neither a DYNAMIC LENGTH item nor an OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY table, so the variable-length-group case falls through to the plain `BoundFieldOperand f => BoundNumLiteral(f.Place.Item.ByteWidth)` arm. The predicate the code needs is the §8.5.1.12.1 one (ANY subordinate dynamic-length elementary item or dynamic-capacity table) and it does not exist in the model; that structural predicate is the fix, not a fourth pattern arm. SIBLING TO SWEEP: BindLengthFold carries the identical guard and the identical hole for §15.50.4 r7. Editions per the AR-15.14.3-1 derivation.

subject: CONCAT function
notes: 'StrArgList(ic) => string.Join(", ", ic.Args.Select(Str))' renders every argument in SOURCE ORDER into one 'Concat(params string[] parts) => string.Concat(parts)' call, a left-to-right fold — the iterated form §15.18.4 r4 prescribes (each concatenation's result becomes argument-1 of the next iteration). Concatenation is associative and no iteration truncates (the intermediate is not a fixed-size receiver anywhere in the model), so the flat n-ary call and the iterated model produce the identical value at every argument count. The TYPE consequence of the iteration was worked through explicitly and adds nothing beyond r2/r3: for every legal mix, the iterated result category (r3 applied per iteration with the intermediate as argument-1) equals the flat reading — e.g. CONCAT(alphabetic, alphabetic, alphanumeric) is alphanumeric both ways — so no r4-specific defect exists; the r2/r3 mislabelling is carried on those rows and is open there. Re-verified on the built CLI for this review: 'FUNCTION CONCAT("A", "B", "C", "D", "E")' → 'ABCDE'; 8 arguments → '1234567AB'; 'FUNCTION CONCAT("a" "b" "c")' → 'abc' and the explicitly nested 'FUNCTION CONCAT(FUNCTION CONCAT("a" "b") "c")' → the same 'abc'; and the §15.3 variable-repetition ALL subscript 'FUNCTION CONCAT(A TE(ALL))' over '05 TE PIC X(2) OCCURS 3' → 'AB P1P2P3', i.e. one implicit argument-2 per occurrence, left to right, which is r4's trigger reached through a single written argument. subject: CONVERT function
notes:
SUSTAINED - exhaustiveness re-derived, then confirmed BY EXECUTION rather than by reading. Citation validated (--check 15.19.3 "The source-format shall be different from the destination-format" -> OK, rule 3). The source-format space is {ANY, ANUM, HEX, NAT} and the destination space is {ANUM, ANUM HEX, NAT, NAT HEX, BYTE}, so the only pairs that can be the SAME format are ANUM->ANUM and NAT->NAT with no HEX - which is exactly `(src==1 && dst==1 && !hex) || (src==3 && dst==3 && !hex)`. ANUM -> ANUM HEX must NOT be diagnosed and is not (15.19.4 NOTE 3 a depends on it, and the corpus golden AH=41 pins it). ANY and BYTE cannot appear on both sides; a bare HEX destination is not in the format and is rejected earlier by the pair check (verified: CONVERT(WS-A ANUM HEX) and CONVERT(WS-A HEX HEX) both -> COBOLNET1514 'not a valid source-format destination-format pair'). "+" : "-") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours).ToString("00") + Math.Abs(t.Offset.Minutes).ToString("00"). InvariantCulture pins the proleptic Gregorian calendar and ASCII digits (positions 1-4). DELIMITED BY SIZE contributes exactly 21 characters - so no receiver scale hides a layout defect. VERIFIED BY DIRECT EXECUTION OF THE SHIPPING METHOD (loaded src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/Cobol.Net.Runtime.dll and invoked CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDate.Format21 over fixed DateTimeOffsets, since TimeZoneInfo.Local reads the Windows registry and ignores TZ): +05:45 -> '2026073010331564+0545', -09:30 -> '...-0930', +12:45 -> '...+1245', 00:00 -> '...+0000', -12:00 -> '...-1200', +13:00 -> '...+1300'. So positions 20-21 (the prior pass's unverified edge (b)) are CORRECT for non-zero minute offsets, position 17 is correct on BOTH branches including the 'same as UTC' => '+' boundary, and the '-' branch of 18-19 cannot exceed 12 because no TimeZoneInfo zone is below -12:00. THE ONE OPEN POINT, now demonstrated rather than suspected: +14:00 -> '2026073010331564+1400'. 15.21.3 positions 18-19 state 'If character position 17 is '+', two numeric digits are returned in the range 00 through 13', and Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours) is UNCLAMPED, so a run on a host whose TimeZoneInfo.Local is 'Line Islands Standard Time' / Pacific-Kiritimati (UTC+14, a zone Windows and IANA both ship) returns '14' there. notes: OVERTURNED FROM PARTIAL. The prior adjudication called the VALUE half CONFORMS after sampling only SMALL out-of-range arguments (0, -5, 3067672) — exactly the PB5 failure mode. THE RANGE GUARD IS UNREACHABLE FOR ANY ARGUMENT OF MAGNITUDE >= 2^63, so the value half DIVERGES too. Root cause, read out of the emitter rather than sampled: IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt renders every integer-kind argument as `(long)(<Int128 expr>)`, an UNCHECKED C# narrowing that WRAPS modulo 2^64 BEFORE CobolDate.DateOfInteger's `if (integerDate is < 1 or > 3067671)` ever sees the value. Generated C# from the repro below, verbatim: `CobolDate.DateOfInteger((long)(Int128.Parse("18446744073709695567")))`. CONCRETE FAILING INPUT, ACTUALLY RUN (E:/Temp/.../scratchpad/doi-refute/q2.cob, q3.cob): `01 P PIC 9(18) VALUE 184467440737096955.` / `01 R PIC 9(18).` / `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER(P * 100 + 67)` — the argument value is 18,446,744,073,709,695,567 = 2^64 + 143,951 — prints 000000000019950215 (i.e. 1995-02-15) under --std 85, 2002, 2014 AND 2023, and prints the SAME thing with `>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON` in effect. §15.5.2 (cite.py --check 15.5.2 OK): 'It shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to the value of FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE (99991231), which is 3,067,671'; §15.3 (cite.py --check 15.3 OK): 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist.' The EC is never set, so neither the implementor-defined default (0) nor the fatal checked raise happens — the function silently returns a PLAUSIBLE WRONG DATE. That the guard works for a small argument is proved by the control run: DATE-OF-INTEGER(3067672) with checking ON aborts with 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): DATE-OF-INTEGER argument 3067672 outside 1..3,067,671', so the divergence is precisely the pre-guard truncation, not a missing EC mechanism. The literal form `FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER(18446744073709695567)` and a `PIC 9(20)` operand reproduce it identically at 2002+; the arithmetic-expression form above reaches it at COBOL-85 as well, because §8.8.1.2 r7 (cite.py --check 8.8.1.2 OK) is explicit that 'Arithmetic expressions allow the user to combine arithmetic operations without the restrictions on composite of operands and receiving data items', so the 18-digit COBOL-85 literal cap does not protect the 85 edition. Second wrap witness: DATE-OF-INTEGER(36893488147419246903) = 2*2^64 + 143,671 prints 19940511. THE SECOND HALF ALSO FAILS, as the prior report found and I confirm: 'a value in integer date form' carries §15.6 Table 21's argument type Int (cite.py --check 15.6 OK: '| DATE-OF-INTEGER | Int1 | Int | Standard date equivalent (YYYYMMDD) of integer date in argument-1 |') = §15.3 type 6 'An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified' (cite.py --check 15.3 OK). FIX SHAPE — TWO FIXES, NOT ONE: (1) the pre-guard truncation is the ROOT and it is NOT specific to this function — IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt feeds DAY-OF-INTEGER, INTEGER-OF-DATE, INTEGER-OF-DAY, FACTORIAL, TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD, TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD, DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD, DAY-TO-YYYYDDD, YEAR-TO-YYYY, COMBINED-DATETIME and FIND-STRING through the same `(long)` cast, so the range check must move to (or be duplicated in) the Int128 domain, or AsInt must raise EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION itself on an out-of-long value; (2) add ["DATE-OF-INTEGER"] = ('i', "§15.22.3 r1") to IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified and sweep the unscreened siblings DAY-OF-INTEGER §15.24.3 / INTEGER-OF-DATE §15.46.3 / INTEGER-OF-DAY §15.47.3 / FORMATTED-DATE §15.39.3 / FORMATTED-DATETIME §15.40.3 with it. subject: DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD function
notes: SUSTAINED, and verified the way 15.4.1 NOTE 2 says to verify it. The body IS the equivalent arithmetic expression: `return YearToYyyy(date / 10000, off, baseYear) * 10000 + date % 10000;`. YY = FUNCTION INTEGER(argument-1/10000) matches because 15.44.4 r1 makes INTEGER the floor and, for the r1-legal range 1..999999, C# truncating `/` IS the floor; mmdd = FUNCTION MOD(argument-1, 10000) matches for the same nonnegative range. I did not take that on argument: I wrote the equivalent arithmetic expression out in COBOL and compared it to the function through the compiler - `COMPUTE R2 = FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(FUNCTION INTEGER(851003 / 10000), 10, 2002) * 10000 + FUNCTION MOD(851003, 10000)` gives 19851003, equal to `FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(851003, 10, 2002)`, and the YY=1 case (10101, 50, 2026) gives 20010101 both ways. Both 15.23.4 NOTE-1 examples reproduce end to end: (851003, 10, 2002) -> 19851003 and (981002, (-10), 1994) -> 18981002; so do the window edges (490101, 50, 1999) -> 20490101 / (500101, 50, 1999) -> 19500101 and the argument-1 endpoints (1, 50, 2026) / (999999, 50, 2026). RECEIVER VARIED, not just the arguments: PIC 9(8), PIC 9(18), PIC 9(12)V99 (-> 19851003.00), PIC 9(10)V9(9) (-> 19999999.000000000), an IF relation condition, a bare DISPLAY of the function-identifier, MOVE to PIC X(8) (-> '19851003') and MOVE to PIC Z(7)9 all give the equivalent-expression value; the only differing case, PIC 9(6)V99 -> 851003.00, is ordinary high-order MOVE truncation, not a rendering defect. The nested reference the 15.23.3 r1 NOTE suggests, FUNCTION TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD(FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(851003, 10, 2002)), returns 0. OBSERVATION (conforming - 15.3 says 'the implementor defines the result of the function reference' when checking is off, though it is inconsistent with DateOfInteger/IntegerOfDate, which return a clean 0): when the delegated YearToYyyy fails an argument rule it returns 0 and the composite yields 0*10000 + mmdd, e.g. (851003, 10, 1600) -> 1003. The argument-screening defects that reach this body are recorded on AR-15.23.3-1/-4/-6, not here.

subject: DAY-OF-INTEGER function
notes:
OVERTURNED FROM PARTIAL TO DIVERGES. 'A value in integer date form' is defined by §15.5.2 ('A value in integer date form is a positive integer ... It shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to the value of FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE (99991231), which is 3,067,671'), and Table 21 (§15.6) types argument-1 'Int1', i.e. §15.3 type 6 ('An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified'). A violation makes §15.3 set EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to exist; the implementor-defined-result latitude in that same paragraph applies ONLY 'if ... checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled'. §7.3.25.4 GR6 says that with '>>TURN ... CHECKING ON' checking IS enabled, so under checking-ON the exception must be raised. It is not, for two whole families of out-of-form argument, and the compiler returns a plausible-looking Julian date instead. That is a WRONG OBSERVABLE RESULT in a context where the spec grants no latitude, not a missing screen.

(1) INT64 WRAP DEFEATS THE §15.5.2 RANGE TEST. IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt emits an UNCHECKED narrowing cast '(long)(<Int128 expr>)' before CobolDate.DayOfInteger's 'integerDate is < 1 or > 3067671' guard ever sees the value, so any argument congruent modulo 2^64 to something in 1..3,067,671 sails through. RAN, at the DEFAULT --std 2023, with checking explicitly ON:
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. DOITURN1.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01 BIG PIC 9(21) VALUE 18446744073709551617.
       01 R PIC 9(7).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON
           COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-OF-INTEGER(BIG).
           DISPLAY "NO EXCEPTION RAISED, R = " R.
           STOP RUN.
prints 'NO EXCEPTION RAISED, R = 1601001'. 18446744073709551617 mod 2^64 = 1, and 1601001 is exactly DAY-OF-INTEGER(1). A second witness, 18446744073709694000 (wrap 142384), prints 1990305. The item itself is undamaged — DISPLAY BIG prints 018446744073709551617 — so the corruption is introduced by the intrinsic argument path alone. Contrast the SAME program with 3067672: it correctly aborts 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): DAY-OF-INTEGER argument 3067672 outside 1..3,067,671'. The prior adjudication tested only that in-range-of-long case and concluded the value half CONFORMS.

(2) A FRACTIONAL ARGUMENT IS NOT A POSITIVE INTEGER (§15.5.2) AND STILL RAISES NOTHING. IntArg silently truncates through NumRescale/Truncation. RAN, checking ON: '01 FR PIC 9(7)V9 VALUE 143951.7.' + 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-OF-INTEGER(FR).' prints 'NO EXCEPTION RAISED, R = 1995046' — identical to the integer 143951.

(3) THE CLASS SCREEN IS ABSENT (the prior finding, still true). DAY-OF-INTEGER is in NEITHER IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified NOR DeliberatelyUnscreened, so CheckArgumentClasses returns at its 'if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;' guard and COBOLNET1627 never fires: 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-OF-INTEGER(A).' with '01 A PIC X(4) VALUE "ABCD"' compiles clean at --std 2023 and prints 0000000. The precedent is one row away — COMBINED-DATETIME's §15.17.3 r1 carries the identical 'shall be in integer date form' wording and IS screened ('n').

(4) A CLASS-NUMERIC FLOATING ARGUMENT EMITS RAW ROSLYN (the PB2 failure mode, unfixed for the 'i' date rows). '01 DVAL USAGE COMP-2.' + 'MOVE 143951 TO DVAL.' + 'COMPUTE R = FUNCTION DAY-OF-INTEGER(DVAL).' fails with "error CS0117: 'CobolIntrinsics' does not contain a definition for 'DayOfIntegerReal'" — an internal failure escaping as a backend error. IntrinsicRenderer routes on AnyRealArgument for EVERY exact arm, but IntrinsicRealArgDriftTests.NumericArgumentMethods scopes its guard to ArgKinds containing 'n', so the 'i' rows (DAY-OF-INTEGER, DATE-OF-INTEGER, INTEGER-OF-DATE/DAY, FACTORIAL, CHAR, the Y2K trio) are unguarded — and the class screen this row is missing would not have caught it either, since 'i' admits CLASS numeric and a COMP-2 IS class numeric (§8.5.2.1 Table 2).

ROOT CAUSE AND SWEEP (CLAUDE.md rule 4): defect (1) is in IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt, which every 'i'-kind arm shares, so it is a PATTERN, not a DAY-OF-INTEGER bug. Confirmed on a sibling in the same run: 'COMPUTE R8 = FUNCTION DATE-OF-INTEGER(BIG)' with checking ON prints 16010101, no exception. The fix is a range/representability check on the Int128 value BEFORE the narrowing cast (or an Int128-typed runtime parameter), plus the row ["DAY-OF-INTEGER"] = ('i', "§15.24.3 r1") in Verified, plus a DayOfIntegerReal body (or a rejection) for the float path.

notes: SUSTAINED, re-verified rather than inherited. DayOfInteger computes 'Epoch.AddDays(integerDate - 1)' from 'Epoch = new DateTime(1601, 1, 1)', which is the §15.5.2 mapping (integer date 1 = Monday 1601-01-01); .NET's DateTime is the proleptic Gregorian calendar §15.5.1 demands over the whole 1601..9999 range. Independent sweep: generated 62 integer dates (the §D.31.3.7 worked example 143951; the endpoints 1 and 3,067,671; the 1700/1800/1900 non-leap and 2000/2400 leap century boundaries at Feb 28 / Mar 1 / Dec 31; 2000-02-29; and 25 pseudo-random in-range values), computed the expected YYYYDDD in Python's proleptic Gregorian calendar from the spec definition alone, and diffed against the compiled program: ALL 62 MATCH. Receiver axis varied too (the PB5 lesson), all correct at 1995046 for argument 143951: PIC 9(7), 9(9), 9(18), S9(9) COMP, S9(9) BINARY, 9(7)V99, 9(9)V9(5), COMP-1, COMP-2, PIC ZZZ9999 via MOVE, plus a receiver-less IF condition, an EVALUATE subject, a direct DISPLAY, and the operand of '+ 1'. subject: DAY-OF-INTEGER function
notes: SUSTAINED; both halves of the rule independently re-verified. 'return d.Year * 1000L + d.DayOfYear;' places the Gregorian year in the YYYY positions and the ORDINAL day of that year in DDD — the §15.5.4 Julian date form ('The Julian date form is YYYYDDD, where YYYY represents the year and DDD represents the ordinal date within that year'). YYYY half: 1 -> 1601001 (epoch year), 3067671 -> 9999365 (terminal year), 143951 -> 1995046. DDD half, over the 62-value spec-computed sweep described in RV-15.24.4-1: the leap-day ordinal is counted (2000-02-29 -> 2000060) and 366-day years reach 366 (2000-12-31 -> 2000366), while the century non-leap years do not (1900-12-31 -> 1900365, 1700-03-01 -> 1700060 vs 2000-03-01 -> 2000061), so §15.5.1's Gregorian leap rule is honoured in the DDD positions and not merely in YYYY. Identical at --std 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023. Coverage note (not a test-need for this row): the cited test's only DAY-OF-INTEGER expectation is 01601001, whose DDD is 001 — no on-disk spec-derived case reaches a leap-day or a three-digit ordinal, which is why the DDD half was checked by running rather than by trusting the suite.

subject: DISPLAY-OF function
notes: UPHELD after varying the RECEIVER as well as the argument. Repertoire appends exactly one character per input character (a substitution replaces, never expands or drops), so the returned string's length is always argument-1's character count, and under D-N1 one national position is one UTF-16 char and one usage-display position. RAN MYSELF at --std 2023: FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(PIC N(5))) -> 005; the same over a PIC N(3) containing a SUBSTITUTED U+4E16 -> 003, so substitution does not change the length; the ZERO-LENGTH national literal FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N"") -> LENGTH 000 and an all-space receiver, which is correct since 15.26.3 carries no zero-length-literal prohibition (its 15.66.3 r3 twin does); a SUPPLEMENTARY-plane national literal in a PIC N(2) -> LENGTH 002 and '??', consistent with the declared D-N1 one-code-unit-per-position model; a reference-modified argument N-SRC(1:3) -> 3; a national GROUP of two PIC N(2) items -> 4. Receiver variation: STRING FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-SRC) DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO a PIC X(10) prefilled with '-' gives [HELLO-----], i.e. exactly 5 positions transferred; MOVE to a PIC X(6) gives 'HELLO '; and the length consequence in comparison is right in both directions - the result compares EQUAL to "HELLO", to "HELLO   " and to a PIC X(8) item, so the shorter operand is space-padded per 8.8.4.1.1 rather than compared as a raw .NET string. subject: E function
notes: Verdict SURVIVES; the note is corrected and the SPEC BASIS the adjudicator missed is supplied. test-needed. Citations re-validated: cite.py --check 15.27.3 'standard-binary arithmetic is in effect' -> OK (rule 2). THE PRECONDITION CAN NEVER HOLD IN THIS COMPILER, re-verified by me on the built CLI: DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects the mode with COBOLNET0806 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature (ISO 8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL' - a HARD error at --std 2002 (alongside COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'), 2014 and 2023, and NOT downgradable by --permissive (2023 adds the COBOLNET0903 obsolescence warning and still errors). Nothing in the tree computes 14114126198520207781233383725636853 / (2 ** 112); CobolIntrinsics.E() is the only body and is Math.E in every mode. WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED, and it is what makes this an owner DECISION rather than a bug: the standard itself classes this clause as processor-dependent. Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim - cite.py --check A.3 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' -> OK - and 4.5 NOTE, validated verbatim ('These factors can include the use of optional, processor-dependent, or implementor-defined language elements'), together mean a conforming implementation may fail to translate a compilation group that uses it without ceasing to conform. Annex F.2 additionally makes STANDARD-BINARY an obsolete feature, and the standard's own Annex E remark records that it 'has not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider'. The non-support is already recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 2 ('| 2 | ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1); the native/standard-decimal modes are provided |') - the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, a verdict only the owner may set, hence NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. BARE QUESTION: should 15.27.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by the existing documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY (Annex A.3 item 2 processor-dependence) rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? Identical to the already-adjudicated sibling RV-15.73.3-2 for PI; one decision should settle the whole 15.4.1 family. EDITIONS DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY OF INTRINSICCATALOG: the STANDARD-BINARY keyword of the ARITHMETIC clause is a COBOL-2014 addition (the 2002 clause offered NATIVE and STANDARD only; the compiler's own edition gate agrees - 'OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY.' at --std 2002 draws COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)', re-run by me), so the rule's precondition cannot arise at 85 or 2002. TEST COVERAGE: none - no test references FUNCTION E under any arithmetic mode. The honest cover is a negative case pinning that FUNCTION E under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is refused BY MODE; a mode-only rejection test that never names E would not cover this row.

subject: EXCEPTION-FILE function
notes:
OVERTURNED from CONFORMS. r1a and r1b hold; r1c is WRONG for two kinds of file connector, and the adjudication missed it by varying the exception ORIGIN while holding the connector KIND fixed at 'ordinary program file'.
WHAT HOLDS (re-run, not inherited). r1a: EcFunctions.File returns "00" when LastName is null or !ExceptionCatalog.IsIoName(name); ran `A=[00]` before any I-O, and also after `SET LAST EXCEPTION TO OFF` following a real 10-status READ (`B=[00]`, EXCEPTION-STATUS blank) -- correct, because 14.6.13.1.1 says the last exception status persists until re-raised or SET-cleared, so a later SUCCESSFUL statement must NOT reset it. r1b: ExceptionEngine.Set() nulls LastFile and only SetIo() populates it, so a NAMED raise structurally cannot carry a connector; ran `RAISE EXCEPTION EC-I-O-AT-END` after a 10-status READ -> `B=[  ]` with EXCEPTION-STATUS still EC-I-O-AT-END (genuinely the r1b branch, not r1a).
WHAT DIVERGES -- r1c, validated: cite.py --check 15.28.4 "exactly as specified in the SELECT clause" -> OK (15.28.4 1) c)), and the printed page 844 reads "The succeeding characters contain the file-name exactly as specified in the SELECT clause". The implementation does not carry the SELECT spelling: it recovers a display name by string surgery on the RUNTIME CONNECTOR KEY -- EcFunctions.File takes `file.LastIndexOf("::")` and returns everything after it. That key is an emit-side namespacing artifact, and for two connector kinds it is not the file-name.
FAILING INPUT 1 -- an OO per-object instance file. BinderDriver.QualifyClassFiles gives an OBJECT-paragraph file the key `Class::INST::NAME` and FileRegistry.MintInstanceKey then appends `#N`, which the `::` strip does not remove:
       >>TURN EC-I-O CHECKING ON
       ... PROGRAM-ID. REFOOF1. REPOSITORY. CLASS OFCLSR. 01 T USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE OFCLSR.
           INVOKE OFCLSR "NEW" RETURNING T.  INVOKE T "DOIT".  STOP RUN.
       CLASS-ID. OFCLSR. ... OBJECT. ... FILE-CONTROL. SELECT OFile ASSIGN TO "refoo-obj.dat".
       FD OFile. 01 OFILE-REC PIC X(12).
       METHOD-ID. DOIT. ... OPEN OUTPUT OFile / WRITE / CLOSE / OPEN INPUT OFile / READ OFile / READ OFile
           DISPLAY "NOARG=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE "]".
ACTUAL `NOARG=[10OFile#1]` -- EXPECTED `NOARG=[10OFile]`. The SELECT clause says `OFile`; `#1` is the runtime's per-object key counter leaking into a user-visible function result.
FAILING INPUT 2 -- an EXTERNAL file. DataBinder.cs sets `file.ExternalName = name.ToUpperInvariant()` and BinderDriver keys the connector `::EXT:: + ExternalName`, so the SELECT spelling is destroyed before the strip ever runs:
       >>TURN EC-I-O CHECKING ON
       ... SELECT ExtF ASSIGN TO "refext1.dat".  FD ExtF IS EXTERNAL.  01 EREC PIC X(5).
           OPEN OUTPUT ExtF / WRITE / CLOSE / OPEN INPUT ExtF / READ ExtF / READ ExtF
           DISPLAY "NOARG=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE "]".
ACTUAL `NOARG=[10EXTF]` -- EXPECTED `NOARG=[10ExtF]`. Both the SELECT and the FD spell it `ExtF`; nothing in 13.18.22 licenses folding the case of the returned string, and 15.28.4 r1c says "exactly as specified in the SELECT clause". That the implementation ALREADY takes spelling seriously elsewhere is the proof this is a defect and not pedantry: for an ordinary file `SELECT MyFile` + `FD MYFILE` correctly yields `10MyFile` (ran).
ROOT CAUSE (one rule, one place): the SELECT-clause spelling is a property of the FileModel and must be carried to the runtime connector as its OWN field, not re-derived by parsing a key whose format is owned by three different qualification sites (PROG::, ::EXT::, Class::INST::+#N, Class::FACT::, Class::SORT::). Every future key-shape change silently re-breaks 15.28.4 r1c/r2b the way ::INST:: and ::EXT:: already have.
Test coverage: the cited test exists on disk, is spec-derived (AssertSpec, expected "F: 10TF" computed from 9.1.13.1 status 10 + the SELECT name) and pins the ORDINARY-file r1c leg only. test-needed for r1a, for r1b, and for both failing legs above -- tests/conformance/2002/exception_file_n.cob covers the analogous 15.29.4 legs of the -N twin, a different function and clause, so it does not count here.

       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.

           SELECT Readf  ASSIGN TO "refef1c.dat" FILE STATUS IS FS2.
       DATA DIVISION.

       01 R2 PIC X(10).
       FD Readf.
       01 R3 PIC X(10).
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

           DISPLAY "EFC=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE(Closed) "]".

EXPECTED: FS1=[42] FS2=[47] EFC=[42Closed] EFR=[47Readf]
The two FILE STATUS values prove both connectors were attempted to be accessed and DO hold an I-O status, so r2a's condition is false for both and r2b governs. Root cause is the flag's DEFINITION, not the two call sites: EverAccessed belongs on the one status-setting path every connector operation passes through, not on a hand-maintained per-verb list that makes the next verb wrong by default.
DEFECT 2 (new, same rule, different half) -- r2b's returned NAME is wrong for the same two connector kinds as 15.28.4 r1c, because FileRegistry.ExceptionFile recovers the display name by the identical `LastIndexOf("::")` surgery on the runtime key. Ran and confirmed: an OO per-object instance file `SELECT OFile` gives `ARG=[10OFile#1]` (the MintInstanceKey `#N` counter leaks) where r2b requires `10OFile`; an EXTERNAL file `SELECT ExtF` / `FD ExtF IS EXTERNAL` gives `ARG=[10EXTF]` (DataBinder.cs uppercases ExternalName) where r2b requires `10ExtF`. So r2b fails on BOTH connector kinds even when EverAccessed is correctly true.
OPEN READING on r2b, unresolved and needing an owner eye (NOT scored as a third defect): the implementation reports the connector's CURRENT I-O status, while 15.28.1 frames the argument form as the status "associated with the last exception status for that file-name" (validated: cite.py --check 15.28.1 "associated with the last exception status for that file-name" -> OK). subject: EXCEPTION-FILE-N function
notes: The rule has TWO requirements and only the first is enforced. BindExceptionFileArg resolves argument-1 with `ctx.Data.Files.FirstOrDefault(f => f.CobolName.Equals(name, OrdinalIgnoreCase))` and issues COBOLNET1574 when nothing matches, so 'shall be the name of a file connector' is screened; 'that is specified in an FD statement' (ISO §15.29.3 rule 1) is NOT screened at all — the lookup filters on neither FileModel.IsSortMerge nor FileModel.HasFd, both of which the model already carries. TWO concrete illegal programs compile with NO diagnostic (run with src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe, default --std 2023; source at E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/40a0808e-7312-48f6-807b-5112b1d817cf/scratchpad/refute/r2.cob): (1) `SELECT SRTF ASSIGN TO "rfn002s.tmp".` + `SD SRTF.` + `01 RSRT PIC X(5).` then `DISPLAY "SD=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N(SRTF) "]".` prints `SD=[  ]` — an SD (sort-merge file description entry, ISO §13.4.6) is not an FD statement, so §15.29.3 rule 1 is violated and must be diagnosed; (2) `SELECT NOFD ASSIGN TO "rfn002n.txt".` with NO FD and NO SD anywhere then `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N(NOFD)` prints `NOFD=[  ]` — likewise undiagnosed, and note that FileModel.HasFd's own doc comment asserts 'a SELECT with no FD is an error the front-end already diagnoses', which this run shows is FALSE (the independent ISO §12.4.5.2 SR3 requirement — 'For each file-name specified in a SELECT clause, there shall be a file description entry or a sort-merge file description entry' — is also unenforced; that is a separate row, but it is why HasFd cannot be assumed true here). The fix is a filter on the ONE resolver: `f.HasFd && !f.IsSortMerge`. SIBLING: the same arm serves FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE (§15.28.3 rule 1) — sweep both. SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME ARM: the COBOLNET1574 message hard-codes 'ISO §15.28.3 rule 1' for BOTH functions, so an EXCEPTION-FILE-N violation is handed the wrong clause (observed on r6.cob: `error COBOLNET1574: FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N argument 'WS-ITEM' is not the name of a file connector specified in an FD statement (ISO 15.28.3 rule 1)`); for EXCEPTION-FILE-N the clause is §15.29.3 rule 1. The 'argument-1 is optional' half IS honoured (0-arg, empty-parens and 1-arg forms all accepted; 2 args rejected COBOLNET1504). EXCEPTION-FILE-N appears in neither IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified nor DeliberatelyUnscreened — behaviourally right (argument-1 is a file-connector-name, not a class-bearing operand, and BindExceptionFileArg returns before CheckArgumentClasses) but it leaves the PB1 drift test blind to this row; it belongs in DeliberatelyUnscreened with the §15.29.3 reason. test-needed: a negative spec-derived case for an SD argument-1, a negative case for a SELECT-without-FD argument-1, and a case pinning COBOLNET1574 with the §15.29.3 clause.

subject: EXCEPTION-FILE-N function
notes: OVERTURNS the CONFORMS. r1a and r1b are correct, but r1c is NOT: §15.29.4 r1c requires 'The succeeding characters contain the file-name exactly as specified in the SELECT clause converted at runtime to the runtime national character set' (cite.py-checked), and EcFunctions.File() does not carry that name — it DERIVES it from the runtime connector KEY by stripping everything up to the last '::' (`int sep = file.LastIndexOf("::"); string display = sep >= 0 ? file[(sep + 2)..] : file;`). That key is an emit-side namespace, and for two legal file kinds it is NOT the SELECT spelling. (1) An OBJECT-paragraph (per-instance) file connector: BinderDriver.QualifyClassFiles rewrites CobolName to `Class::INST::NAME` and FileRegistry.MintInstanceKey appends `"#" + N`, so the key is `OFCLS8::INST::OFILE#1` and the strip yields `OFILE#1`. Actually run (scratchpad/refute/r8.cob, --std 2023, a CLASS-ID with an OBJECT FILE-CONTROL `SELECT OFILE ASSIGN TO "rfn008.dat".`, two READs to end-of-file under >>TURN EC-I-O CHECKING ON): observed `NOARG=[10OFILE#1]` with `LEN=009`; §15.29.4 r1c requires `10OFILE` with FUNCTION LENGTH 7. The returned value contains two characters ('#','1') that are not part of the file-name at all — '#' is not even in the COBOL word repertoire — so this is not a case quibble, and the length is wrong too. (2) An EXTERNAL file connector: BinderDriver rewrites CobolName to `"::EXT::" + ExternalName` where ExternalName is set in DataBinder.BindFileSection as `name.ToUpperInvariant()`, so the strip yields the UPPERCASED FD-derived externalized name (ISO §13.18.22.4 GR5), not the SELECT spelling. Actually run (scratchpad/refute/r7.cob): `SELECT MixedExtFile ASSIGN TO "rfn007.dat" FILE STATUS IS WS-FS.` + `FD MixedExtFile IS EXTERNAL.` gives `NOARG=[10MIXEDEXTFILE]`, `LEN=014`; r1c requires `10MixedExtFile`. That the ordinary case is right (scratchpad/refute/r1.cob: `SELECT MixedCaseVeryLongFileNameXY` + `FD MIXEDCASEVERYLONGFILENAMEXY` -> `FN=[10MixedCaseVeryLongFileNameXY]`, LEN=029, SELECT spelling preserved exactly) proves the intended reading and makes the EXTERNAL/OBJECT paths an inconsistency, not a design choice. ROOT CAUSE (one rule written in two places): the SELECT-spelled DISPLAY name is being recovered from the DISPATCH key, so every future key band ('::EXT::', '::INST::', '::FACT::', '::SORT::', the '#N' mint) silently corrupts a §15.28/§15.29 returned value. The structural fix is to carry the SELECT-spelled name as its own registry/connector field (set once from FileModel at registration) and delete both LastIndexOf('::') strips — one field, and the NEXT band is automatic. SIBLING: identical defect in §15.28.4 r1c (FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE) through the same EcFunctions.File(), and in §15.29.4 r2b / §15.28.4 r2b through FileRegistry.ExceptionFile's own copy of the strip — sweep all four. VERIFIED-GOOD halves: r1a — EcFunctions.File() returns "00" when ExceptionState.LastName is null or !ExceptionCatalog.IsIoName(name) (StartsWith "EC-I-O"), projected national by CobolIntrinsics.NationalOf; golden tests/conformance/2002/exception_file_n.out shows `PRE=00` / `LEN-PRE=02`. r1b — ExceptionEngine.Set() nulls LastFile and only SetIo() sets it, so all three listed origins return two national spaces; I ran the EXIT leg myself (scratchpad/refute/r5.cob, `EXIT PROGRAM RAISING EXCEPTION EC-I-O-AT-END` in a nested program after a real status-10 READ: sub-program shows `SUB-EFN=[10TF]`, activator shows `AFTER-CALL=[  ]`, `LEN=002`, `ST=EC-I-O-AT-END`), and `GOBACK RAISING LAST EXCEPTION` correctly does NOT take the r1b path (scratchpad/refute/r3.cob -> `AFTER-CALL=[10TF]`, LEN=004 — the RAISING phrase specifies no exception-name, so r1c applies). The result category is national and lengths are counted in character positions (golden `NAT=YES` against N"10TF", `LEN-FN=04`). The cited conformance-test is spec-derived and exercises r1a + the ordinary r1c; it does not reach either divergent file kind, and r1b has no spec-derived test. test-needed: a 2023 case pinning EXCEPTION-FILE-N over an EXTERNAL file connector and over an OBJECT-paragraph file connector, plus an r1b case.

subject: EXCEPTION-FILE-N function
notes: BOTH halves of rule 2 diverge — the prior adjudication called r2b 'verified-good', and that is wrong. (A) r2a is over-broad. §15.29.4 r2a returns two national spaces only when the connector 'has never been opened, attempted to be opened, or otherwise attempted to be accessed' (cite.py-checked). FileConnector.EverAccessed — the ONLY flag FileRegistry.ExceptionFile tests — is written in exactly two places: FileConnector.Open and FileRegistry.DeleteFile. A READ / CLOSE / WRITE / START / REWRITE / DELETE against a never-opened connector IS an attempted access: ISO §9.1.13 makes those the very statements that set the connector's I-O status, so r2b must apply. Concrete failing input, actually run (scratchpad/phaseb3/t7.cob, --std 2023): `SELECT INF ASSIGN TO "efnacces.txt" FILE STATUS IS WS-FS.` + `FD INF.` + `READ INF AT END CONTINUE END-READ.` on a never-opened file -> `FS-AFTER-READ=47` but `EFN=[  ]`; then `CLOSE INF.` -> `FS-AFTER-CLOSE=42` but `EFN2=[  ]`. Expected per r2b: `EFN=[47INF]`, `EFN2=[42INF]` — the FILE STATUS item proves the I-O status was set, i.e. the connector was attempted to be accessed. Fix: set EverAccessed on every connector-touching verb, or better, derive it from 'the I-O status has ever been assigned' so the next verb is automatic. (B) r2b returns the WRONG file-name for two legal file kinds — the same root cause as §15.29.4 r1c. FileRegistry.ExceptionFile builds the name by `name.LastIndexOf("::")` over the runtime connector KEY, but that key is an emit-side namespace. Actually run: for an OBJECT-paragraph (per-instance) file (scratchpad/refute/r8.cob, `SELECT OFILE ...` inside an OBJECT paragraph) `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE-N(OFILE)` returns `ARG=[10OFILE#1]` — the per-object mint suffix from FileRegistry.MintInstanceKey (`baseKey + "#" + N`) leaks into the returned value; r2b requires `10OFILE`. For an EXTERNAL file (scratchpad/refute/r7.cob, `SELECT MixedExtFile ...` + `FD MixedExtFile IS EXTERNAL.`) it returns `ARG=[10MIXEDEXTFILE]`, the uppercased ISO §13.18.22.4 GR5 externalized name, where r2b requires the SELECT spelling `10MixedExtFile`. SIBLING: both defects are shared verbatim with §15.28.4 r2a/r2b (FUNCTION EXCEPTION-FILE) through the same FileRegistry.ExceptionFile — sweep both, and fold the r2b half into the ONE display-name fix described on RV-15.29.4-1. test-needed: there is NO spec-derived test for the EXCEPTION-FILE-N argument form at all (tests/conformance/2023/exception_file_arg.cob is the alphanumeric EXCEPTION-FILE); a 2023 case is needed covering r2a (never accessed), r2a-vs-r2b (attempted-but-never-opened), r2b over an ordinary FD, r2b over an EXTERNAL FD and r2b over an OBJECT-paragraph file.

subject: EXCEPTION-LOCATION function
notes:
VERDICT SURVIVES; one root-cause claim CORRECTED and a FIFTH defect added. Re-verified correct: r2a (no exception raised, or after SET LAST EXCEPTION TO OFF -> one space, FUNCTION LENGTH = 1); the string is genuinely variable-length (LENGTH = 20 for 'REFZ1; MAIN-PARA; 13') and behaves as an ordinary alphanumeric sending operand under both a wide (PIC X(50), space-filled) and a narrow (PIC X(5), truncated) receiver; r2b part 1 for a PROGRAM-ID; and - not checked before - r2b part 1's SECOND SENTENCE, the propagated case: a nested PROGRAM-ID REFP1SUB raising EC-USER-L and returning by plain GOBACK reports 'L=[REFP1SUB; SUB-PARA; 14]' in the activator, i.e. the element in which the condition actually occurred (ref/p1.cob). r2b part 2b (paragraph alone, and paragraph + ' OF ' + section) is correct.

FIVE DEFECTS, all reachable from EcBinder.EcLocation and its inputs:

(1) r2b part 2a - 'If there is no paragraph-name or section-name in the source element, a semicolon and a space character are appended.' EcLocation reads `ctx.Table.Paragraphs[ctx.BindCursor].Cobol` unconditionally and ProcedureTableBuilder.AddAnonymousParagraph names the SS14.4.3 paragraph-name-OMITTED paragraph '(sentences without a paragraph-name)', so that internal display label leaks into the returned value. Ran (ref/e2.cob):
       >>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFE2.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-L.
           DISPLAY "M=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION "]".
           STOP RUN.
EXPECTED 'M=[REFE2; ; 5]'; ACTUAL 'M=[REFE2; (sentences without a paragraph-name); 5]'.

(2) r2b part 2c - 'If there is a section-name and no paragraph-name, the section-name is appended followed by a semicolon and a space character.' Ran (ref/e3.cob), a section header followed directly by unnamed sentences:
       >>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFE3.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       ONLY-SECT SECTION.
           RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-L.
           DISPLAY "L=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION "]".
           STOP RUN.
EXPECTED 'L=[REFE3; ONLY-SECT; 6]'; ACTUAL 'L=[REFE3; (sentences without a paragraph-name) OF ONLY-SECT; 6]'.

(3) NEW - and it CORRECTS the earlier claim that the 2c branch 'is unreachable'. The 2c branch IS reachable; it is simply keyed on the wrong predicate. EcLocation selects it with the heuristic `sec is not null && para.Equals(sec, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)`, which fires whenever a real paragraph happens to be NAMED the same as its containing section - legal COBOL (SS8.4.2.2 SR7 bars a duplicate paragraph-name only WITHIN a section; nothing bars a paragraph-name equal to a section-name, and the paragraph here is never explicitly referenced). Ran (ref/e1.cob):
       >>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFE1.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       ONLY-SECT SECTION.
       ONLY-SECT.
           RAISE EXCEPTION EC-USER-L.
           DISPLAY "L=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION "]".
           STOP RUN.
There IS a paragraph-name, so r2b part 2b applies and the section-name must be appended prefixed by ' OF '. EXPECTED 'L=[REFE1; ONLY-SECT OF ONLY-SECT; 7]'; ACTUAL 'L=[REFE1; ONLY-SECT; 7]' - the required ' OF ' + section-name is silently dropped. So the ONE heuristic is wrong in BOTH directions: it never fires where 2c is required and it fires where 2b is required. The structural fix (rule 5) is to make the anonymous paragraph carry an explicit 'no paragraph-name' FLAG on the procedure table instead of a display label, and to select 2a/2b/2c from that flag plus the section, deleting the name-comparison heuristic entirely.

(4) r2b part 1 for a METHOD. 'The name of the runtime element as specified in the FUNCTION-ID, METHOD-ID, or PROGRAM-ID paragraph of the ... method ... containing the statement' (a method is a runtime element, SS10.5). Verified by reading: OoDriver.BindClassBody calls `binder.ConfigureEc(session.Turn, cls.Name)` for the whole method roster (and again for the factory roster), EcBinder.ConfigureEc stores it in `ctx.EcState.ProgramName`, and grep shows EcState.ProgramName is assigned in exactly ONE place - so no method can ever supply its own METHOD-ID name. A CLASS-ID MyCls containing METHOD-ID DoIt whose M-PARA raises reports 'L=[MyCls; M-PARA; 9]' where r2b part 1 requires 'L=[DoIt; M-PARA; 9]'.

(5) The GOBACK / EXIT PROGRAM ... RAISING path captures NO location at all under WITH LOCATION. Verified by reading and by running. `public sealed record BoundRaising(string? EcName, bool IsLast, bool Fatal, bool Enabled, Place? ObjectSource = null)` has no WithLocation/Location member - unlike BoundRaise and BoundEcChecked - and ExceptionState.SetPropagating(name, fatal) calls `Set(name, fatal)`, the two-argument overload that leaves LastLocation null. Ran (ref/p2.cob):
       >>TURN EC-USER CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFP2.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           CALL "REFP2SUB".
           DISPLAY "S=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS "]".
           DISPLAY "L=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION "]".
           DISPLAY "T=[" FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT "]".
           STOP RUN.
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. REFP2SUB.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION RAISING EC-USER-L.
       SUB-PARA.
           GOBACK RAISING EXCEPTION EC-USER-L.
       END PROGRAM REFP2SUB.
       END PROGRAM REFP2.
ACTUAL 'S=[EC-USER-L ...]' (so the last exception status DOES indicate a raised condition and r2a does not apply) but 'L=[ ]'; EXPECTED 'L=[REFP2SUB; SUB-PARA; 15]'. SS7.3.25.4 GR6 puts the file-level >>TURN in scope for the nested program's statements and GR7 then requires the information to be made available. Sibling on the same path: FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT is 63 spaces (SS15.32.3 r2).

A SIXTH way to get a wrong r2 result comes from RV-15.30.3-1's per-statement WITH LOCATION collapse: an r2b-shaped string is produced for a condition whose own enabling directive specified no LOCATION, where neither r2 nor r1's save branch licenses one.

subject: EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N function
notes:

r2 a) IS correct (LocationN returns NationalOf(" ") when LastName is null). r2 b) fails four ways.

CAUSE: ExceptionEngine.SetPropagating(name, fatal) calls Set(name, fatal) with the `statement` and `location` parameters DEFAULTED TO NULL.

(4) NEW -- the NONFATAL ambient EC gates never carry location at all. EcEmitter.EmitChecked wraps them in a bare set/reset with NO catch (correct -- nonfatal never throws), so the only writer is the runtime helper, and ExceptionEngine.BoundOverflowError / DataConversionError call `Set(name, fatal)` with statement/location defaulted null. RAN:
       >>TURN EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. RELNQ1.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

(5) READ FROM CODE, NOT RUN: r2 b) 1. requires "the name of the runtime element as specified in the FUNCTION-ID, METHOD-ID, or PROGRAM-ID paragraph". OoDriver.BindClassBody calls `binder.ConfigureEc(session.Turn, cls.Name)` for both method rosters, so EcBinder.EcLocation's `ctx.EcState.ProgramName` is the CLASS-ID for a statement inside a METHOD, never its METHOD-ID.

subject: FACTORIAL function
notes:
OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> DIVERGES, and the test-ref is WITHDRAWN. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.36.3 "Argument-1 shall be an integer greater than or equal to zero."` => OK §15.36.3 1). The completing rule is §15.3 (`--check 15.3` OK at item 14: 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument or for the returned value ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist ... and checking ... is not enabled, the implementor defines the result'), and §14.6.13.1.6 classifies EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION as **Fatal**, so with checking enabled the run unit must terminate.
WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED — THE RULE IS ENFORCED AGAINST A VALUE THAT IS NOT THE ARGUMENT. It read `CobolIntrinsics.Factorial(long n)`'s `n is < 0 or > 33` guard and called half A 'IMPLEMENTED'. That guard runs on the result of `IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt`, which is `(long)({a.Expr})` when Scale==0 and `(long)(CobolNum.Rescale(...))` otherwise. Both operands are Int128: `PicInfo.ElementType` is `Digits > 18 ? "Int128" : "long"`, `EmitText.IntLiteral` emits `Int128.Parse("...")` past 18 digits, `CobolNum.Rescale` returns Int128, and `CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric` returns Int128. `RoslynBackend.Compile` passes `new CSharpCompilationOptions(OutputKind.ConsoleApplication, optimizationLevel: Release, nullableContextOptions: Disable)` and NEVER sets checkOverflow, so the generated C# is UNCHECKED and `(long)` on an Int128 SILENTLY WRAPS modulo 2^64. §8.3.3.3.2 (`--check` OK) requires fixed-point literals of 1..31 digits, and `EditionContext` accepts 19..31-digit pictures/literals at 2002+ — so an argument of 2^64 + k is CONFORMING source under §15.36.3 r1 (it is an integer >= 0) and arrives at the guard as k. The guard therefore approves it, and §15.4's returned-value-length EC is never reached either. This is the PB5 shape exactly: an extreme magnitude the adjudicator never sampled. See defect 1.
HALF B (integer-ness) CONFIRMED ABSENT, and its consequence is a §15.3 divergence rather than a mere gap: `CheckArgumentClasses` opens `if (!IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified.TryGetValue(sig.Name, out var rule)) return;` and I confirmed by reading the whole table that FACTORIAL is in NEITHER `Verified` (which holds ABS, ORD, ORD-MAX, ORD-MIN, PRESENT-VALUE, RANDOM, RANGE, REM, REVERSE, SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME, PI, ACOS, ASIN, ATAN, ANNUITY, CHAR, CHAR-NATIONAL, BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER, COMBINED-DATETIME) NOR `DeliberatelyUnscreened`. So (i) a class-ALPHANUMERIC operand is coerced by `CobolNum.FromAlphanumeric`, whose body is literally `foreach (char c in image) if (c is >= '0' and <= '9') mag = mag * 10 + (c - '0');` (defect 3), and (ii) a class-numeric NON-INTEGER operand is truncated by `AsInt`'s Rescale-with-Truncation arm and NO EC is set even with checking ON (defect 4). §15.3 says the condition 'is set to exist'; it is not. A required fatal condition that never fires on non-conforming input is active divergence, not absence.
TEST-REF WITHDRAWN. `IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests#OutOfDomain_EcDefaultZero_PinnedToSpec` IS an `AssertSpec` (not `*MatchesLegacy`, not nist/characterization) and does contain `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION FACTORIAL(0 - 1). DISPLAY R.` expecting `+000000`. But the spec derives only 'EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is set and, checking off, the implementor defines the result' — the specific value is not spec-derived, and the test's own comment says so: 'the legacy-compatible default the goldens encode'. Under the brief's rule 3 that is corroboration for one leg (checking OFF, negative argument, native arithmetic), not a spec-derived test, so the field is left empty. Everything else is untested: checking ON (must terminate), a non-integer argument, an alphanumeric argument, a >18-digit argument, any argument under STANDARD/STANDARD-DECIMAL, and the compile-time-known `FUNCTION FACTORIAL(-1)` literal form (the existing test writes `0 - 1`, an expression, so the literal path is unexercised).
EDITIONS: derived as for FMT-15.36.2 — 2014/2023 mechanical (Table 21 + absent from the 2023 added/enhanced list + absent from Annex E); 85/2002 are the project's 1989-amendment convention and are NOT checkable against specs/ISO_COBOL.md. Never read from the IntrinsicCatalog row. The truncation defect itself is scoped 2002,2014,2023 because 19+ digit pictures/literals require --std 2002 (EditionContext).

subject: FIND-STRING function
notes: CONFIRMED at the floor, plus a finding the adjudicator missed. Citation re-run: `cite.py --check 15.37.3 "argument-3 shall be an integer data item or integer literal"` → OK §15.37.3 rule 3. The rule is NARROWER than §15.3 type 6 (which admits 'an arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value'): r3 admits only a DATA ITEM or a LITERAL. Neither half is checked. BindFindString calls BindArgOperand, which binds the whole arithmeticExpression alternative; IntrinsicRenderer.IntArg→AsInt then emits, for a non-zero scale, `(long)(CobolNum.Rescale(…, Truncation))` — a SILENT truncation. So `FUNCTION FIND-STRING(H N 1.9)` compiles clean and behaves as skip=1, and `FUNCTION FIND-STRING(H N (A + B))` compiles clean though the rule bars an expression. ⚠ NEW — THE CATALOG ROW IS ITSELF WRONG AND WOULD ENFORCE THE WRONG CLASS THE MOMENT THE SCREEN IS MADE REACHABLE: IntrinsicCatalog declares FIND-STRING with MinArgs 2 / MaxArgs 3 but `ArgKinds = "sssii"` — FIVE per-position codes for a three-argument maximum. `IntrinsicSig.ArgKind(i) => ArgKinds[Math.Min(i, ArgKinds.Length - 1)]`, so ArgKind(2) — argument-3 — reads 's' (alphanumeric/string) where §15.37.3 r3 makes it an INTEGER, and the trailing 'ii' is unreachable. The row has never been contradicted because ArgKind has no caller on this path: a dead lookup is also an unverified one. Fixing the reachability defect must therefore NOT simply switch this function on against ArgKinds. And a Verified row cannot carry r3 either — 'i' in that table means §15.3's integer TYPE, which deliberately admits numeric-edited de-editing and arithmetic expressions, exactly what r3 excludes. r3 needs its own arm in BindFindString.

notes: REFUTED UP FROM PARTIAL. The prior pass verified the VALUE half and called the TYPE half merely 'unscreened'; reading the EMISSION path shows the type half is worse than unscreened - it emits a call to a runtime method THAT DOES NOT EXIST, so conforming source fails to compile. (1) THE VALUE HALF STILL HOLDS: CobolDate.IntegerOfDate decomposes yyyymmdd by /10000, /100%100, %100 and rejects year outside 1601..9999 (subrule a), month outside 1..12 (subrule b) and day <1 or >DateTime.DaysInMonth (subrule c); the || short-circuits so DaysInMonth only sees an in-range year/month, and .NET's proleptic Gregorian matches Sec 15.5.1 ('The date conversion functions shall use the Gregorian calendar as described in ISO 8601-1:2019, 4.2.1' - --check verified) over the whole window. Violations route to ExceptionState.ArgumentError -> EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION when checking is enabled, else the Sec 15.3 item-14 implementor-defined 0 ('If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference' - --check verified against Sec 15.3, item 14). (2) NEW, AND THE REASON THIS IS DIVERGES - THE FLOATING-POINT ARGUMENT PATH EMITS A NONEXISTENT METHOD. If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference."

THE VALIDATION ITSELF IS CORRECT and I re-read every leg: CobolDate#Analyze walks the tokenized format against the data, requiring each in-data separator ('-', ':', 'W', 'T', 'Z') to appear, rejecting a non-digit, a short field and any trailing character (`if (pos != data.Length) return pos + 1;`), and range-checking every subfield with per-digit narrowing - year 1601..9999 (§15.3.1.3/.5/.7, "greater than 1600 and less than or equal to 9999"), month 1..12, day-of-month against DaysInMonth, day-of-year against the leap year, week against LongIsoYear, weekday 1..7. I checked LongIsoYear against §15.3.1.7's OWN formulation (53 weeks "if the year subfield represents a common year and January 4 of that year falls on Sunday, or if the year subfield represents a leap year and January 4 of that year falls on a Saturday or Sunday") and derived that it is equivalent to ISO 8601's Jan-1-Thursday / leap-Wednesday rule, which is what ISOWeek.GetWeeksInYear implements - so the week cap is right. A nonzero result becomes ExceptionState#ArgumentError, which I read: it sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION fatal when checking is enabled and otherwise returns 0 - exactly §15.3 rule 14's disposition.

Every §15.3.1.7 subfield rule passes for both: 9999 > 1600 and <= 9999; 9999 is a 52-week ISO year so week 52 is inside 01..52; day-of-week 6 and 7 are inside 1..7. So "YYYYWwwD"/"9999W526" AND "YYYYWwwD"/"9999W527" are both PERMISSIBLE DATA that abort the run unit with a raw CLR stack trace - neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition, where §15.3 rule 14 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result. THE TIME PORTION IS GENUINELY VALIDATED, and I checked the two subtle legs against the spec text rather than trusting the comments. §15.3.3.2 says of the BASIC common time format with fractional seconds that "the decimal separator does not appear in the data", and of the EXTENDED form that "the two colon characters and the decimal separator appear in the data" - Tokenize's `bool extended = fmt.IndexOf(':') >= 0 || fmt.IndexOf('-') >= 0;` and its `segs.Add(new(false, default, 0, c, extended))` for '.'/',' implement exactly that split, and Annex D.31.5.8's own worked data "19950215T05142781+0500" (no '.' present, against the format "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm") corroborates it. §15.3.3.3 gives hour 00..23, minute 00..59 and seconds ">= 00 and < 60 when the LEAP-SECOND directive with the OFF phrase is in effect" - Analyze's (0,23)/(0,59)/(0,59) match under the only mode this compiler supports. The mandatory 'T' (§15.3.3.7) and the 'Z' marker (§15.3.3.5) are in-data separator segments that must appear; the offset sign is restricted to '+'/'-'/'0' with §15.3.3.6.1's zero-sign-implies-zero-magnitude narrowing; offset hour 0..23 and offset minute 0..59; and the trailing `pos != data.Length` check bars a short or over-long argument-2. It does not, for the primary branch of the 12.3.7 format 'LOCALE locale-name-1 IS { external-locale-name-1 | literal-4 }': (a) LOCALE is not a lexer token -- zero hits for LOCALE across all of src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/, and the LOCALE phrase of LOWER-CASE etc. is matched on TEXT by IntrinsicBinder#HasLocalePhrase -- so it lexes as IDENTIFIER; (b) specialNameEntry ends in two catch-all alternatives, implementorSwitchEntry ( cobolWord (IS cobolWord)? ... ) and genericClause ( IDENTIFIER (IDENTIFIER|literal)* ), and cobolWord admits IDENTIFIER; so 'LOCALE FR-LOC IS EXT-NAME' decomposes into entries that both catch-alls accept; (c) the ONLY two consumers of specialNameEntry in the whole compiler are DataBinder.Switches#SwitchBindSpecialNames and MnemonicRegistry#Of, and BOTH silently 'continue' past everything they do not recognise -- there is no unknown-entry diagnostic. Net effect: the clause is SILENTLY ACCEPTED and MnemonicRegistry registers EXT-NAME as a device mnemonic bound to FR-LOC, usable afterwards in e.g. DISPLAY ... UPON EXT-NAME. Only the literal-4 branch ('IS "fr_FR"') is a parse error, because IS followed by a literal starts no entry. This (i) violates A.4.1 ('An implementation shall accept the syntax ... for an optional element only when support ... is claimed'), (ii) contradicts the owner's own decision-3 requirement of UNIFORM not-supported diagnostics, and (iii) contradicts docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 4 item 5, which tells the user this entry point is a parse error. It is a compile-clean, run-time-invisible acceptance -- the PB7 shape -- and it is NOT covered by PB1-PB11/PB13. SIBLING SWEEP (same A.4.9 item 10, same silent shape): 'ALPHABET a1 IS LOCALE [locale-name-2]' takes the alphanumeric branch, where AlphabetOperands maps an unrecognised bare word through '_ => t' and feeds the letters L,O,C,A,L,E into the collating table -- silently accepted AND a silently WRONG alphabet; the FOR NATIONAL branch does reject it, but as COBOLNET0898 'not a supported code-name (12.3.7.3 SR15)', never citing A.4.9. DOT)?` (CobolParserCore.g4 line 379) with `computerAttributes : ~(DOT | PROGRAM)+` (line 397) - a raw-token SINK. Nothing in CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION IS <locale-phrase> is a DOT or a PROGRAM, and grep finds ZERO occurrences of CLASSIFICATION in src/Cobol.Net.Frontend or src/Cobol.Net.Compiler, so the whole clause is swallowed and discarded. X CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION IS USER-DEFAULT.` compiles with no diagnostic at all - and note that the SYSTEM-DEFAULT / USER-DEFAULT / LOCALE alternatives of locale-phrase-1 (12.3.6.2) need no SPECIAL-NAMES locale-name, so this is a complete, self-contained request that a locale BE in effect for character classification - after which every FUNCTION LOWER-CASE quietly returns the rule-4 implementor-defined invariant fold instead of the LC_CTYPE mapping the source asked for. ⚠ NEW, FROM RENDERING THE FORMAT: the 12.3.6.2 figure note states the outer bracket encloses CHOICE INDICATORS, so per 5.2.6.4 the CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION and PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE clauses may appear 'in either order'. notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. The original adjudication sampled MIDDLE-OF-RANGE outputs (12.34 / -5.00 / 99.99; FLOAT-LONG 2.5 vs 7.25; INDEX 4 vs 9) and read the mechanism as correct. Reading the implementation instead finds THREE independent, probe-confirmed defects, each producing a silently wrong returned value on CONFORMING source, and none of them reachable from the values sampled. ALSO: TWO CITATIONS IN THE ORIGINAL RECORD ARE WRONG, one level off in the way this review has been burned by before - the record cited 'NUMERIC (§8.8.4.2.2, algebraic value)' and 'INDEX (§8.8.4.2.3)'; `cite.py --check 8.8.4.2.2 "For operands whose class is numeric, a comparison is made with respect to the algebraic value of the operands"` FAILS, because §8.8.4.2.2 is 'General format' and §8.8.4.2.3 is 'Syntax rules'. The real clauses are §8.8.4.2.4 (Comparison of numeric operands, --check OK) and §8.8.4.2.13 (Comparisons involving index-names or index data items, --check OK). §8.8.4.2.7 / §8.8.4.2.9 in the record are correct. THE THREE DEFECTS: (D1) THE SCALE-ALIGNMENT WIDENING WRAPS Int128 SILENTLY. AlignedArgsEx picks s = max(argument scales) and emits NumericRenderer.Align -> `CobolNum.Rescale(x, from, s, Truncation)`, whose widening arm is a bare `value * Pow10Wide(toScale - fromScale)`; RoslynBackend sets no checkOverflow, so any argument needing more than 38 digits at the common scale wraps modulo 2^128 BEFORE MaxScaled ever compares it. PIC 9(21) against PIC 9V9(18) - both far inside the 31-digit standard range and both accepted by the compiler's own data description - needs 39 digits and wraps NEGATIVE, so MAX returns the SMALLER argument. This is the PB5/PB13/PB22 unchecked-narrowing family in its widening direction, and AlignedArgs feeds MIN, SUM, RANGE, MEDIAN, MIDRANGE, ORD-MAX and ORD-MIN identically - sweep it. NO ARITHMETIC-MODE LATITUDE IS AVAILABLE: it reproduces verbatim under `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.`, where §8.8.4.2.4's native sentence does not apply and the standard instead requires the comparison to be performed as if each operand were converted to a standard-decimal intermediate data item - which both operands fit. (D2) A SINGLE FLOAT ARGUMENT DESTROYS EVERY OTHER ARGUMENT'S CONTENT. AnyRealArgument routes the whole call to RenderFloat, which renders every argument as a C# double and calls `MaxReal(params double[] xs) => xs.Max()`, then quantizes with FromDouble. §15.59.4 r1 says the returned value IS THE CONTENT of the selected argument - not an approximation of it, and §15.59.4 carries no equivalent arithmetic expression, so §15.4.1's native-arithmetic latitude ('the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor', --check OK) does not reach the VALUE. Mixing a FLOAT-LONG item with a fixed-point item is conforming source: §8.5.2.1 Table 2 puts both under class Numeric, so §15.59.3 r2 is satisfied. The selection is CORRECT (ORD-MAX and the relation condition both name the fixed argument) and the delivery is wrong by eighteen orders of magnitude. (D3) A NATIONAL GROUP ARGUMENT IS COMPARED WITH THE ALPHANUMERIC COLLATING SEQUENCE. §8.5.2.1 says 'a national group item has class and category national' (--check OK) and §8.8.4.2.9 requires national operands to compare by the current NATIONAL program collating sequence (--check OK). But OperandCategory returns `f.Place.Item.IsGroup ? null : ...`, so nationalArg is FALSE for a national group; BindIntrinsicCore then sets `collate = maxMinStr && ctx.Data.Collating is not null && !nationalArg` = TRUE and the backend passes the 256-entry ALPHANUMERIC __COLLATE weights table over national characters - precisely the aliasing the code's own CHAR/ORD comment says must never happen. Two MAX calls over identical national data return OPPOSITE answers depending only on whether the data is described as an elementary item or as a national group. WHAT IS CONFIRMED CORRECT (and is why this is DIVERGES on boundaries, not NOT-IMPLEMENTED): fixed-point comparison inside 38 aligned digits; the alphanumeric native and PCS paths through CobolString.Compare with §8.8.4.2.7 r2 space padding, never string.CompareOrdinal; and the elementary-national path. Test-ref cleared: conformance:2002/intrinsic_max_collating is spec-derived and remains valid corroboration for the alphanumeric-PCS leg, but a green test cannot close a DIVERGES row. NEW FIX-QUEUE ITEM covering D1 (with the AlignedArgs family sweep), D2 and D3. EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only; D1/D2/D3 all reproduce at --std 85/2002/2014/2023. D1: wide2.cob (RFMAXWID2) `01 B1 PIC 9(21) VALUE 999999999999999999999. 01 B2 PIC 9V9(18) VALUE 0.000000000000000001. 01 RB PIC 9(21).` -> `COMPUTE RB = FUNCTION MAX(B1 B2)` prints B21x18=000000000000000000000 (must be 999999999999999999999) and `FUNCTION MIN(B1 B2)` prints MINB=020847100762815390391 - a value equal to NEITHER argument's content, which is the wrap made visible. The same file's in-range control `01 C1 PIC 9(29)` against `01 C2 PIC 9V9(9)` (38 aligned digits) prints C29x9=99999999999999999999999999999, correct - so the boundary is exactly Int128's 38 digits. wide.cob (RFMAXWIDE) PIC 9(30) vs PIC 9V9(9) -> WIDE=000000000000000000000000000000. widerel.cob (RFMAXWREL) shows the shared root cause: `IF B1 > B2` prints REL=B1-NOT-GT-B2, so the relation condition wraps too. widestd.cob (RFMAXWSTD), identical but with `OPTIONS. CITATION FIX: the original note said '§8.8.4.2.2 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value'; §8.8.4.2.2 is 'General format' and --check FAILS on that text. The clause is §8.8.4.2.4 (--check OK: 'For operands whose class is numeric, a comparison is made with respect to the algebraic value of the operands regardless of the manner in which their usage is described ... Zero is considered a unique value regardless of the sign'). WHY THIS SURVIVES THE ATTACK AT IMPLEMENTATION LEVEL RATHER THAN BY SAMPLING: leftmost-wins is a property of ExtremeIndex ALONE - `for (int i = 1; i < xs.Length; i++) { int c = cmp(xs[i], xs[k]); if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0) k = i; }` - and is independent of the comparator passed in, so it holds identically for all six MaxString/MinString overloads (native pad-compare, the ushort[] alphanumeric-PCS weights, and the NationalCollation variant) and for OrdMaxString/OrdMinString, which is the whole family in one place. The original evidence only exhibited SAME-CONTENT / DIFFERENT-LENGTH ties, which cannot distinguish leftmost-wins from a stable comparator; the refuter added a tie between DIFFERENT CONTENTS of EQUAL VALUE, which is what the rule is actually about, and it passes on the weights overload. The NUMERIC/INDEX half remains vacuous rather than unverified, and the argument is sound: §8.8.4.2.4 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value (and makes signed and unsigned zero one value), §15.59.4 r3 confines the SIZE question to alphanumeric and national, and under standard arithmetic §15.4.1 puts the returned value in a mode-defined intermediate data item whose characteristics come from the mode rather than from the selected argument - so two tied numeric or index arguments have no observable difference in content to choose between. CONTINGENCY WORTH RECORDING: this rule governs which of the TIED arguments is returned; whether the tie is real is RV-15.59.4-1's question, and at the boundaries documented there the 'greatest value' premise is itself wrong. notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The rule is a CONDITIONAL - 'IF THE TYPE OF THE FUNCTION IS alphanumeric or national, the size of the returned value is the same as the size of the selected argument-1' - and it therefore has two halves: the antecedent (deciding the function type, per the §15.59.1 result-type table) and the consequent (the size). The original adjudication verified the CONSEQUENT thoroughly and treated the ANTECEDENT as settled by the V54 fix. THE ANTECEDENT IS MISDECIDED FOR A WHOLE ARGUMENT SHAPE. §8.5.2.1 states 'a national group item has class and category national' (--check OK), so §15.59.1's table gives a NATIONAL function type for national-group arguments. BindIntrinsicCore decides the type with `category = args.All(a => OperandCategory(a) is PicCategory.National) ? National : Alphanumeric`, and OperandCategory is `BoundFieldOperand f => f.Place.Item.IsGroup ? null : f.Place.Item.Pic?.Category` - NULL for every group. So MAX over national group items is typed ALPHANUMERIC, and the rule's own antecedent selects the wrong branch: the returned size is then expressed in alphanumeric rather than national character positions, and the §14.9.25 Table-16 National->AN MOVE guard that the V54 fix installed is bypassed for exactly the shape it was written to catch. The CONSEQUENT itself is confirmed correct in every shape reachable: MaxString returns `xs[ExtremeIndex(...)]`, i.e. the SELECTED element of the params array, so the returned string is the selected argument's own rendered image and carries its own width - nothing re-pads it and no compile-time size is imposed. What is NOT closed is the antecedent for group arguments, and that is why this is PARTIAL and not CONFORMS. The fix belongs with the RV-15.59.4-1 D3 item (same OperandCategory null-for-group root cause, same one-line consequence for both the collating sequence and the result category), not as a separate queue entry. ⚠ The Alphanumeric fallback on a MIXED national/alphanumeric argument list is a different defect and belongs to AR-15.59.3-2 (such a list is not conforming source).
