subject: MEAN function
notes:
REFUTED — THE "WHAT CONFORMS" HALF IS FALSE. The previous record certified the fixed-point half as conforming on the strength of "the exact Int128 sum (identical to the SDIDI addition chain — ≤32-digit sums are exact in both engines)" and "probed TRUE for n=1, 2 and 3". Both are sampling artefacts of small operands, exactly the PB5 mistake the brief names. The premise is wrong: what enters SumScaled is not the arguments, it is the arguments RESCALED to their common scale by AlignedArgsEx → NumericRenderer.Align → `CobolNum.Rescale`, whose widening arm is a bare unchecked `value * Pow10Wide(toScale - fromScale)` over Int128. A 31-digit integer argument beside a scale-18 argument aligns to 10^49, and Int128 tops out at 1.70e38, so the operand WRAPS MODULO 2^128 before SumScaled or CobolDec.From ever sees it.

THE HARD DIVERGENCE (no implementor latitude anywhere in it). Under `OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL.` at --std 2023, with FIXED-POINT arguments ONLY and no float in the program:
    01 WS-A PIC 9(31) VALUE 1000000000000000000000000000000.
    01 WS-B PIC 9V9(18)  VALUE 2.0.
    IF FUNCTION MEAN(WS-A WS-B) = (WS-A + WS-B) / 2  →  FALSE
    COMPUTE WS-R = FUNCTION MEAN(WS-A WS-B)  →  0000000000009480057455463682825
    COMPUTE WS-R = (WS-A + WS-B) / 2         →  0500000000000000000000000000001   ← correct, same compiler, same mode
§15.4.1 r1 is unconditional under the standard modes ("the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression") and NOTE 2 states the relation "will evaluate to true". It evaluates FALSE, and the compiler's OWN evaluation of §15.60.4's expression proves the correct value is reachable: the SDIDI sum is 1000000000000000000000000000002 (31 significant digits, well inside §8.8.1.5.2 NOTE 2's 34-digit precision) and the quotient 500000000000000000000000000001 is exact. §15.4.1's implementor-defined escapes do not reach this — it is not native arithmetic, no argument is implementor-defined, and no sub-expression produces implementor-defined results.

LEGALITY OF THE WITNESS (checked before relying on it): the 31-digit composite limit is §14.7.7 r2, which binds only "ADD, DIVIDE, MULTIPLY, and SUBTRACT statements when native arithmetic is in effect" — not COMPUTE, and not a relation condition, and not any standard mode (§14.7.7 r3 defines statements under the standard modes in terms of arithmetic expressions instead). So the witness is legal source in every statement it uses.

SAME DEFECT UNDER NATIVE, and no size error to warn anyone: the identical program with no OPTIONS paragraph returns 0000000000007534060890583240347 for a true mean of 500000000000000000000000000001 that FITS the PIC 9(31) receiver exactly, with the ON SIZE ERROR phrase present and NOT taken. §8.8.1.3 makes native arithmetic implementor-defined and §15.4.1 asks only for "an implementor-defined approximation", but a value 11 orders of magnitude away, produced by a silent modulo-2^128 wrap, is not an approximation of anything and is not a technique the implementor has specified. Note also that native and standard-decimal wrap to DIFFERENT garbage (7534060890583240347 vs 9480057455463682825), so the "same value for a given function" property of §15.4.1 fails as well.

EDITION WINDOW OF THE HARD DIVERGENCE: reproduced under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD` at --std 2002 (STD-NOTE2 FALSE, MEAN=9480057455463682825 against a correct EAE) and under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` at --std 2023. `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY` is loudly refused (COBOLNET0806, citing §8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F), so §15.4.1 r1's standard-binary half is unreachable rather than wrong — that is a separate, already-loud disposition, not this row's.

SIBLING SWEEP (⌘ rule 4). AlignedArgs feeds every variadic exact-family arm, so the wrap is theirs too — probed on the SAME operands at --std 2023: MAX = 18960114910927365649 and SUM = 18960114910927365651 (both should be 1000000000000000000000000000000 / 1000000000000000000000000000002), MIDRANGE = 9480057455463682825. §15.59.4/§15.88.4/§15.62.4/§15.61.4/§15.76.4 all inherit it, and MOD/REM take the same Align at line 109-116. ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN answered correctly here only by luck of the wrapped ordering.

FIX SHAPE (⌘ rule 5 — the structural answer, not the smallest diff): the alignment is the wrong mechanism. Under the standard modes each argument must be lifted into SDIDI individually (`CobolDec.From(unscaled, ownScale)`) and summed/divided there — 34 digits, and the mode already owns the rounding — instead of being forced to a common Int128 scale first. Under native, `CobolNum.Rescale`'s widening arm and `CobolNum.Divide`'s `num *= Pow10Wide(exp)` need the same treatment PB22 gave the narrowing cast: a range check that RAISES rather than an unchecked multiply that wraps. A drift test over (argument digits + common scale) > 38 keeps it true.

STILL STANDING FROM THE PREVIOUS RECORD (re-verified, not inherited): the FLOAT-ARGUMENT divergence. RenderNum's `if (AnyRealArgument(ic) && sig.RuntimeMethod != "Factorial") return RenderFloat(ic, RealMethod(...))` fires BEFORE the switch, so a COMP-2 argument (class numeric, therefore a legal §15.60.3 argument) routes to CobolIntrinsics.MeanReal — a double accumulate + divide — REGARDLESS of the arithmetic mode, while the expression side lifts through CobolDec.FromDouble. §8.8.1.5.2 r1 is unconditional and §15.4.1 r1 then requires equality; it does not hold. And the DEAD GUARD is confirmed by reading, not by output: the MeanScaled arm's `if (num.StandardDecimal && !anyReal)` computes `anyReal` from AlignedArgsEx with the SAME `num.AsNum(a, num.Receiver).Real` predicate AnyRealArgument used to return at the top of RenderNum, so `!anyReal` is invariantly true there and the flag is unreachable-as-written.

REFUTED (editions, narrowed from "2002, 2014, 2023"): the old window was derived from when the OPTIONS ARITHMETIC clause exists in this compiler, not from the spec, and it also mis-scoped the column — §15.60.4 itself is edition-independent wherever MEAN exists. §15.60 is absent from Annex E and Annex F, which supports 2014 and 2023; the 2023 text establishes nothing for 2002 or 85. The reproduction under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD` at --std 2002 is recorded in the evidence as behaviour, not as a spec-derived window.

DEDUPE FOR THE PARENT: fix-queue PB14 is adjacent (STANDARD/STANDARD-DECIMAL + an intrinsic argument) but its stated symptom is a CS1503 on a Dec-typed argument; neither the Int128 alignment wrap nor the binary64/SDIDI value split is that, so both are reported here rather than assumed covered. EVIDENCE: CITATIONS (every one re-run by the refuter, none inherited): `--check 15.60.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows"` → OK §15.60.4 1). `--check 15.4.1 "the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression"` → OK §15.4.1 1). `--check 15.4.1 "implementor-defined approximation"` → OK §15.4.1. `--check 8.8.1.5.2 "Any operand of an arithmetic expression that is not already in SDIDI form is converted into this form"` → OK §8.8.1.5.2 1). `--check 8.8.1.5.2 "with a maximum precision of 34 decimal digits"` → OK §8.8.1.5.2. `--check 14.7.7 "the composite of operands shall not contain more than 31 digits"` → OK §14.7.7 2) a). `--check 14.7.7 "When standard-decimal or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, each arithmetic statement is defined in terms of one or more arithmetic expressions"` → OK §14.7.7 3). CORRECTED: the previous record cited §8.8.1.5.1 for "implementor-defined"; `--check 8.8.1.5.1 "implementor-defined"` FAILS — the clause is right but its wording is "The mechanisms for conversion of data items described with a usage of float-short, float-long, or float-extended into standard-decimal intermediate data items are defined by the implementor", which --checks OK. §15.60.4 cases a/b/c read directly at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 32246-32260 and match the transcription.

CODE READ (the refuter's primary evidence — implementation, not output):
· IntrinsicRenderer.AlignedArgsEx → `NumericRenderer.Align(x, s)` → `CobolNum.Rescale({expr}, {x.Scale}, {s}, Truncation)`.
· CobolNum.Rescale: `if (toScale > fromScale) return value * Pow10Wide(toScale - fromScale);` — an UNCHECKED Int128 widening multiply. Pow10Wide is documented for n in 0..38; nothing bounds `value × 10^n`.
· CobolNum.Divide: `if (exp >= 0) num *= Pow10Wide(exp);` — the same unchecked widening on the native quotient path, reached with exp = ws − s where ws = max(Receiver.Scale, s+1, 6).
· MeanScaled emits `RuntimeApi.NumDivide(false, …)` — the non-throwing overload is hardcoded, so this multiply is outside the size-error machinery in every context.
· RenderNum: the `AnyRealArgument` early return precedes `switch (sig.RuntimeMethod)`, so `case "MeanScaled"`'s `num.StandardDecimal && !anyReal` guard can never see anyReal true; RealMethod("MeanScaled") = "MeanReal"; CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.MeanReal accumulates `double t` and returns `t / xs.Length`.

The exception half of the rule (alphabetic mixed with alphanumeric) is satisfied trivially and permanently, because PicCategory folds PIC A into Alphanumeric and CobolClass has no Alphabetic member by design — so no future tightening can accidentally reject that legal mixture. notes: REFUTED in scope: verdict DIVERGES stands, but the adjudication found ONE divergence where there are TWO, and named the wrong one as the root cause of the worst behaviour. (a) THE ONE THE ADJUDICATION FOUND, re-verified and correct: the value is materialized at `ws = Receiver.WorkingScale(NumvalScaleFloor)` = clamp(max(receiver scale, 6)) and TRUNCATED there. Under NATIVE arithmetic §15.4.1 licenses it ('the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor'); under STANDARD-DECIMAL it does not -- §15.4.1 requires the returned value be 'contained in a temporary standard data item in the intermediate form defined for the arithmetic mode in effect' and §8.8.1.5.2 gives the SDIDI 'a maximum precision of 34 decimal digits', so NUMVAL("1.2345678") must return exactly 1.2345678. The `case "Numval":` arm never consults the arithmetic mode. (b) THE ONE IT MISSED, and it is worse: `unscaled = unscaled * 10 + (c - '0')` is UNCHECKED Int128 arithmetic (no `checked`, no `<CheckForOverflowUnderflow>` in Directory.Build.props), so past 38 digits the accumulator WRAPS MODULO 2^128 before Rescaled's saturation guard is ever reached. Rescaled's doc comment claims it is 'SATURATING at the Int128 carrier instead of wrapping' and that the saturation is therefore safe -- the invariant is false here, because the guard is on the SHIFT and nothing guards the ACCUMULATE. Measured: a 39-digit argument bearing NO sign character returns a NEGATIVE value, and a receiverless DISPLAY of it renders `--170141183460469231731687303715884.105728` -- a numeric text with TWO minus signs, which is not a valid rendering of any value. So 'the returned value is the numeric value represented by argument-1' fails not by a fraction digit but by sign and by magnitude, and the text channel emits malformed output. notes: The rule has six halves; two are implemented and four are enforced nowhere. IMPLEMENTED: 'Any leading or trailing spaces in argument-2 are ignored' (NumvalC does `currency.Trim()`), and the NOTE's interior-space currency string survives that trim. NOT ENFORCED, all four silently: (a) 'shall be of the same class as argument-1'; (b) 'shall contain at least one non-space character'; (c) 'shall not contain any of the digits 0 through 9'; (d) 'shall not contain ... \'*\', \'+\', \'-\', \',\', or \'.\'; or the two consecutive letters \'CR\' or \'DB\''. notes: Sub-rules b, c, d, e and f CONFORM; sub-rule a — the two general formats, which is the substance of the rule — is not enforced at all. NumvalC is a STRIP-AND-DELEGATE parser: `text.Replace(cur, "")` removes the currency wherever it occurs (any position, any number of times), `Replace(group, "")` removes grouping separators everywhere INCLUDING after the decimal separator, and the residue goes to Numval, which itself admits a leading AND a trailing sign together (its own comment concedes 'Both present is malformed; the lenient double-strip'). No positional scan of either format survives anywhere on the value path, so non-conforming argument-1 yields a plausible value and EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is never set. ROOT CAUSE, and it is the one_rule_one_place pattern: the SAME rule already has a correct positional scanner twenty lines away in TestNumvalC, written for TEST-NUMVAL-C. §15.94.3 r1 makes them literally the same rule and §15.94.1 says TEST-NUMVAL-C exists 'to allow the user to verify that the NUMVAL-C function will produce a valid numeric result' — and the two disagree on four out of four probed strings. The fix is not more strip-and-delegate leniency; it is NumvalC driving the shared scanner (scan-then-value) so one format definition serves both functions. Minor traceability leak of the same delegation: a NUMVAL-C argument failure reports '§15.67.3' (NUMVAL's clause) in its runtime message. Reading the implementation finds two independent ways a CONFORMING argument-1 returns a value that is not the value it represents. (1) UNANCHORED CURRENCY REMOVAL DESTROYS THE SIGN. NumvalC does `text.Replace(cur, "")` — no position, no count — before Numval ever sees the string. §15.68.3 r2 forbids argument-2 from containing 'the two consecutive letters CR or DB' but expressly permits the SINGLE letters, and §12.3.7.3 22) b) shows the standard bans C, D, R, B where it means to (the bare CURRENCY SIGN symbol) — r2 deliberately does not, because r4a matches the currency POSITIONALLY, not by substring removal. So argument-2 'C' with argument-1 'C123.45CR' is fully conforming r4a format B and returns 0.00 where §15.68.4 r1 requires -123.45; likewise 'R'/'R123.45CR' and 'D'/'D123.45DB'. The compiler CERTIFIES these strings itself: FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C('C123.45CR','C') returns 0, which by §15.94.4 1) a) means 'the content of argument-1 conforms to the argument rules for the NUMVAL-C function'. This is not §15.3's implementor-defined result on bad input — it is a wrong value on input the compiler agrees is good. (2) THE RETURNED VALUE IS CHANNEL-DEPENDENT. Every subfield satisfies §15.3.1.7: year 9999 is >1600 and <=9999; Jan 4 9999 is a Monday so 9999 is a 52-week ISO year and week 52 is inside the permitted 01..52; day-of-week 7 is inside 1..7. The expected result is +86399.00 — D.31.5.9 makes the date VALIDATED BUT DISCARDED for this function, so the integer date form is never needed here at all; Analyze computes it unconditionally at its `else if (hasWeek) integerDate = ISOWeek.ToDateTime(...)` leg, and ISO-9999-W52-7 falls on 10000-01-02, outside DateTime.MaxValue. Even on the most conservative reading (that the denoted date is out of range and r5 is therefore violated), §15.3 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result — never a raw CLR stack trace, which is neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition. Sibling sweep (same Analyze line, both verified crashing identically): `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` and `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` — the latter is the worse one, since §15.92 defines TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME as the VALIDATOR that returns an error position and can therefore never legitimately fault. Fix shape: bound-check the week-date reconstruction (and hand SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME a path that does not build integerDate at all). The rest of r5 is correct and was verified: the mandatory 'T' is required in the data (§15.3.3.7); the D.31.5.9 worked example `("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500")` → +18867.81 with the offset correctly excluded; Feb-31 in the same format → the §15.3 default 0; the calendar boundary "99991231T235959" → +86399.00. test-needed. ⚙ FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-08-05 (fix-queue PB23). This row's ONLY divergence was the shared week-date reconstruction, and the row itself said so ("ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX"). CobolDate#Analyze no longer calls ISOWeek.ToDateTime: §15.3.1.7 fixes week 1 as "the week that includes January 4", so that week's Monday is computed directly and every later day is a plain integer offset from it — the arithmetic CANNOT overflow, which is the point, because the input is VALID and no tightening of the per-subfield range table could have prevented the fault. The result is then range-checked against §15.5.2's ceiling ("shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671"), and ONLY the caller that must PRODUCE an integer date form reacts: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError per §15.3 rule 14's "incorrect value ... FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" arm (implementor-defined result 0 when checking is off), while TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME still answers 0 — §15.92.4 requires any non-zero answer to be "the ordinal character position at which the first error ... was detected", and no CHARACTER of "9999W526" is in error (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid) — and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME still returns its seconds (§15.79.4 reads only the time subfields). THE TWO-DAY WINDOW THIS ROW RECORDS (d=6 AND d=7) IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not re-derived on paper: 9999-12-31 is ISO 9999-W52-5. The new arithmetic is proven EQUIVALENT to ISOWeek over >200,000 week dates spanning 1601-9999 by unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.TheIntegerWeekArithmetic_AgreesWithISOWeek_Everywhere, which asserts its own population so it cannot pass vacuously. ⛔ THE TEST GAP THIS ROW NAMED IS ALSO CLOSED: the golden carries Annex D.31.5.8's and D.31.5.9's OWN worked examples — "YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951, and "hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and its combined form both -> 18867.81 — so the §15.48.4 / §15.79.4 NOTE that the other half "does not impact the returned value" is now verified by TEST rather than by code reading.

subject: SIN function
notes: Citation validated: cite.py --check 15.82.4 'The returned value is the approximation of the sine of argument-1 and is greater than or equal to' -> OK (rule 1). Implementation: CobolIntrinsics.Sin(double x) => Math.Sin(x), reached through RenderFloat (the catalog row is Float:true). Both halves of the rule verified: (a) approximation - Math.Sin is the binary64 sine with full argument reduction, and S15.82.4 specifies no equivalent arithmetic expression, so per S15.4.1 the approximation is implementor-defined in EVERY arithmetic mode (native: 'the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor'; the standard-mode returned-value-shall-equal-the-EAE requirement applies only 'when ... an equivalent arithmetic expression is specified', which is why SIN is correctly absent from the ArithmeticStandardIntrinsic loud-stage list); (b) range - Math.Sin returns a value in [-1,+1] for every finite double argument. Receiver handling preserves the bound: a FLOAT or receiverless context keeps the binary64 value through RealResult (NaN - reachable only from a non-finite COMP-2 argument - is screened to the S15.3 EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION default 0 or the raise under checking); a FIXED-POINT receiver quantizes through the one FromDouble at FloatWorkingScale >= 9, and rounding a |v| <= 1 value at scale >= 9 can produce at most exactly +/-1.0, still within the rule's bounds. subject: CURRENT-DATE function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL -> DIVERGES, and a SECOND rejection of legal source the prior pass missed. Citations re-run: cite.py --check 15.21.2 '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>CURRENT-DATE</u>' OK (the prior pass's plain-text form FAILS the checker - the format lives inside the <pre>/<u> markup); 15.21.1 'returns a 21-character alphanumeric value' OK; 8.4.3.2.3 SR2 'the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier' OK; 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 'the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments' OK; 8.4.3.3.3 SR2 'shall reference an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function' OK; 12.3.8.1 'intrinsic-function-names that may be used without specifying the word FUNCTION' OK; 15.23.3 r5 / 15.100.3 r5 '(FUNCTION NUMVAL (FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:4)))' OK. ACCEPTING HALF IS CORRECT: IntrinsicCatalog#Build carries CURRENT-DATE as IntrinsicArity.Fixed 0..0; IntrinsicBinder#BindIntrinsicCore's MinArgs/MaxArgs arm rejects an argument. RAN 'MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CD' (PIC X(21)) at --std 85 and 2023 -> '2026073010394849-0700'; 'MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE(WS-N)' -> 'error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE takes 0 argument(s); 1 given (ISO 15.3)'. DIVERGENCE (a) REFERENCE-MODIFIED FORM REJECTED - ACTUALLY RUN, all four editions: source 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. CDR1. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 WS-YR PIC X(4). PROCEDURE DIVISION. MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:4) TO WS-YR DISPLAY "YR=[" WS-YR "]" STOP RUN.' -> 'CDR1.cob(8,39): error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input '('' + 'error COBOL0001: unexpected '(''. It is legal: 8.4.3.3.3 SR2 permits reference modification of a function-identifier that references an alphanumeric function and 15.21.1 makes CURRENT-DATE alphanumeric; 8.4.3.2.3 SR6's argument-paren preemption is conditioned on 'If a function's definition permits arguments' and 15.21.2's format permits NONE, so the '(' can only be a reference-modifier. The standard writes this exact shape in NORMATIVE text three times - 15.23.3 r5, 15.25.3 r5, 15.100.3 r5 'FUNCTION NUMVAL (FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:4))'. Root cause: CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall is 'FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?' with NO refModPart tail (refModPart exists only in CobolParserCore.g4, reachable only from dataReference). Sibling sweep: 'MOVE FUNCTION UPPER-CASE("abc") (1:2) TO WS-A.' fails identically at col 44, so reference modification of ANY function-identifier is unimplemented. DIVERGENCE (b) NEW - THE KEYWORD-OMITTED ZERO-ARGUMENT FORM SILENTLY COMPILES AND CRASHES AT RUN TIME (missed entirely by the prior pass): source 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. PROGRAM-ID. CDR4. ENVIRONMENT DIVISION. CONFIGURATION SECTION. REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC. DATA DIVISION. WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. 01 WS-CD PIC X(21). PROCEDURE DIVISION. MOVE CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CD DISPLAY "CD=[" WS-CD "]" STOP RUN.' compiles with ZERO diagnostics and then throws 'CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... reference 'CURRENT-DATE'' - reproduced at --std 2002, 2014 AND 2023, and identically with the explicit specifier 'FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE INTRINSIC.'. It is legal: 12.3.8.1 'It also allows declaration of intrinsic-function-names that may be used without specifying the word FUNCTION' + 8.4.3.2.3 SR2; and 8.4.3.2.2's general format makes the whole parenthesized argument list optional, so the bare name IS a complete function-identifier. The standard writes the combined keyword-omitted + reference-modified shape itself at D.14.3.6: 'MOVE FUNCTION LOCALE-DATE (CURRENT-DATE (1:8)) TO a-date-field.'. Root cause is structural and exact - IntrinsicBinder#KeywordOmittedFunction opens with 'var suffixes = dref.dataReferenceSuffix(); if (suffixes.Length != 1 || suffixes[0].subscriptPart() is not { } sp) return null;' so the path is reachable ONLY through a name(args) subscript shape; a ZERO-argument keyword-omitted reference has ZERO suffixes, never reaches IntrinsicCatalog, and falls through to an unresolved data reference (control: an undeclared 'NO-SUCH-NAME' produces the byte-identical loud stage). Sibling sweep: 'COMPUTE WS-P = PI' under FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC fails the same way, so EVERY zero-argument intrinsic (CURRENT-DATE, PI, E, WHEN-COMPILED, RANDOM, the EXCEPTION-* group) is unreachable in the keyword-omitted form. The fix is the suffix-count relaxation plus a zero-argument bind, not a per-function patch. SECONDARY, accepting too much: 'MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE () TO WS-CD' is ACCEPTED and evaluates, but 15.21.2's format carries no parentheses and 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 cannot make that '(' an argument paren for a function that permits no arguments, so it is a malformed reference-modifier and should be diagnosed. TEST COVERAGE: the cited test exists on disk at tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs line 284 and is spec-derived - AssertSpec runs 'new CobolNetCompiler(dialect).CompileAndRun' and Assert.Equal against a literal, no legacy/GnuCOBOL oracle anywhere in the path - and it writes 'FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE' in the bare general-format shape, so it covers the accepting half ONLY. test-needed for (i) the 0-arity negative (COBOLNET1504), (ii) the 8.4.3.3.3 SR2 reference-modified form, (iii) the 12.3.8.1 keyword-omitted zero-argument form. BOOKKEEPING: CURRENT-DATE is absent from IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified; vacuous for a zero-argument function, but PI carries an explicit ["PI"] = (' ', '15.73.2 - no arguments') row for exactly this case, so CURRENT-DATE should carry the twin and keep IntrinsicArgumentClassDriftTests honest.

subject: EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N function
notes:
OVERTURNS the prior CONFORMS. Citations validated: cite.py --check 15.31.2 "FUNCTION" -> OK (General format); 8.4.3.2.3 "the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier" -> OK SR2; 8.4.3.2.3 "If a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows" -> OK SR6; 8.4.3.3.3 "it shall reference an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function" -> OK SR2.

The HAPPY PATH is right and I re-ran it: bare `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N` compiles and runs at --std 2002/2014/2023; one argument is rejected COBOLNET1504 "takes 0 argument(s); 1 given (ISO 15.3)"; --std 85 is rejected COBOLNET1502. But the format's DEFINING property -- that it carries NO argument list -- has two consequences the compiler gets wrong, both RUN.

(1) 8.4.3.2.3 SR2: with the name (or the ALL phrase) in the REPOSITORY paragraph, "the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier". RAN (cobol.exe --run):
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. RELN04.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       CONFIGURATION SECTION.
       REPOSITORY.
           FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           DISPLAY "X=[" EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N "]".
           STOP RUN.
Got   NO compile diagnostic, then at run time: NotImplementedCobolFeatureException "a COBOL feature that is not yet implemented was reached at run time: reference 'EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N'".
Spec  X=[ ] (the 15.31.3 r1 one national space).
Identical with the NAMED specifier `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N INTRINSIC.` (RELN07). ROOT CAUSE, read from code: IntrinsicBinder.KeywordOmittedFunction bails at `if (suffixes.Length != 1 || suffixes[0].subscriptPart() is not { } sp) return null;` -- it recognises the keyword-omitted form ONLY in the shape `name(args)`. A function whose GENERAL FORMAT has no argument list can therefore NEVER be written without the word FUNCTION; the bare word stays a data reference and falls through to a runtime NotImplemented. Proof it is the zero-argument shape and not REPOSITORY support in general: in the SAME REPOSITORY ALL INTRINSIC unit `UPPER-CASE("abc")` -> U=[ABC] and `LENGTH("abcd")` -> L=[4] both work.

(2) 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 treats a following left parenthesis as an argument list only "If a function's definition permits arguments". 15.31.2 permits none, so a `(` after the name can only be a REFERENCE MODIFIER -- which 8.4.3.3.3 SR2 expressly allows here ("If identifier-1 is a function-identifier, it shall reference an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function"; 15.31.1: "The type of the function is national"). RAN:
           MOVE FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N (1:1) TO N2.
Got   error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input '(' / unexpected '('.
Spec  accepted; the unique data item is national position 1.
ROOT CAUSE: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)?` has no reference-modifier alternative at all.

SIBLING SWEEP (both defects are patterns, both confirmed by run): (1) breaks EVERY zero-argument intrinsic under REPOSITORY -- `CURRENT-DATE` bare gives the same runtime NotImplemented, and the same holds for EXCEPTION-LOCATION / EXCEPTION-STATEMENT / EXCEPTION-STATUS / EXCEPTION-FILE / EXCEPTION-FILE-N / E / PI / RANDOM / WHEN-COMPILED. (2) breaks reference modification of EVERY function-identifier -- `FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:8)` and `FUNCTION UPPER-CASE("abcdef") (2:3)` are both COBOL0001, and `FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (1:8)` is one of the most common idioms in real COBOL.

NOT a divergence: `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N ()` is accepted; the 8.4.3.2.2 diagram's ellipsis sits inside the parentheses over a BRACKETED item, and SR6's NOTE writes `FUNCTION MAX (FUNCTION RANDOM () A B)`, so an empty list is derivable -- a leniency at worst.

Editions derived independently of the catalog row: 8.11 Intrinsic function names lists EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N; the exception-condition facility (TURN directive, RAISE, the last exception status) and class national are both COBOL-2002 introductions; no Annex E entry adds or changes EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N for 2014 or 2023 (E.3.3 item 26 touches only EXCEPTION-FILE-N's optional argument). Both cited fixtures verified present on disk and both name EXCEPTION-LOCATION-N.

subject: EXCEPTION-STATEMENT function
notes: OVERTURNED CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Independently re-verified the half the adjudicator got right, then found the half they did not test. VERIFIED: I re-extracted the canonical PDF myself (pypdf, page index 881 = printed page 852) and the printed 15.32.2 carries exactly the two words `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT` -- nothing lost toward false restriction, so the OCR at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 15.32.2 is faithful. Lexing: NAME_BODY (CobolLexer.g4) matches the 19-char EXCEPTION-STATEMENT and beats the 9-char EXCEPTION keyword by maximal munch, so it reaches `functionName : IDENTIFIER`. Arity: catalog row is Fixed 0..0, so IntrinsicBinder COBOLNET1504 rejects an argument list. Edition window re-derived from the SPEC, not the catalog row: 15.32 depends on the last exception status (14.6.13.1.1) and the 7.3.25 TURN directive, both COBOL-2002; EXCEPTION-STATEMENT is not among the 1989 Intrinsic Function amendment functions; `grep EXCEPTION-STATEMENT specs/ISO_COBOL.md` returns NO Annex E and NO Annex F hit, so it is neither new-in-2023 nor archaic -> 2002,2014,2023 stands. WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED -- the claim 'NO legal shape of this format is rejected' is FALSE. 8.4.3.1.2 Format 1 (cite.py --check 8.4.3.1.2 'Format 1 (function-identifier)' -> OK) makes a function-identifier an IDENTIFIER, and 8.4.3.2.3 SR1 (--check OK) bars it only from a RECEIVING operand, so EVERY identifier-N SENDING position admits `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT`. The grammar routes `functionCall` from only four places (CobolExpressions.g4 primaryExpression, CobolParserCore.g4 displayStatement and moveSendingOperand, CobolIO.g4 strUnstrSender). The FROM phrases of WRITE / REWRITE / RELEASE are `FROM (dataReference | literal)` with no functionCall alternative, and FUNCTION is a lexer keyword absent from cobolWord, so `WRITE REC FROM FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT` is a hard PARSE ERROR on legal source -- 14.9.51.4 GR5a (--check 14.9.51.4 'MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1' -> OK) makes that identifier-1 a MOVE SENDING operand. The project's own CobolIO.g4 DA4 comment states the principle ('every identifier-N SENDING position admits one') and then applied it to STRING/UNSTRING only. Filed under defects. The cited test is spec-derived but exercises the format in the DISPLAY position only; there is no negative test on the argument-list rejection and none on the FROM positions.

FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC., INSPECT EXCEPTION-STATUS TALLYING WS-N FOR ALL "-" compiles with NO diagnostic then dies with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: INSPECT of unresolvable item 'EXCEPTION-STATUS'. The four stand.

FOUR NEW LEADS I CHASED; THREE RETRACTED — recorded so nobody re-files them. (a) CALL "SUBX" USING BY CONTENT FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS is rejected (COBOL0001) — RETRACTED as a defect: that is CALL FORMAT 1, and 14.9.4.3 SR3 (validated: cite.py --check 14.9.4.3 "Identifier-2 shall reference an address-identifier or a data item defined in the file, working-storage, local-storage, or linkage section." -> OK) restricts identifier-2 to a DATA ITEM IN A SECTION, which a function-identifier is not, so the rejection is CORRECT. Format 2 (program-prototype) uses identifier-4, which SR17 only makes a sending operand with no section restriction and SR20 discusses as possibly non-receiving — a function-identifier there is arguably legal and I did NOT verify it; that is an open lead, not a finding. (b) SR2 keyword-omitted with a NAMED repository entry (REPOSITORY. FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS INTRINSIC. + bare EXCEPTION-STATUS) WORKS — no gap beyond ALL INTRINSIC. (c) EXCEPTION-STATUS is NOT in the §8.9 reserved-word list (that list carries EXCEPTION and EXCEPTION-OBJECT only; EXCEPTION-STATUS/-FILE/-LOCATION/-STATEMENT appear only in the §8.11 intrinsic-function-name list), so `01 EXCEPTION-STATUS PIC X(5)` alongside `FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS` must both work — I ran it and BOTH work (D=[HELLO] / F=[31 spaces]). (d) The empty-parenthesis leniency FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS () is CONFORMING, not laxity — I read the printed §8.4.3.2.2 diagram in the transcription (the bracketed argument-1/OMITTED item sits INSIDE the parenthesized group, and the figure note says "the whole parenthesized argument list is optional"), and the §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 NOTE literally writes `FUNCTION MAX (FUNCTION RANDOM () A B)`.

EDITION WINDOW RE-DERIVED FROM THE SPEC, NOT FROM THE CATALOG ROW: §8.11 lists EXCEPTION-STATUS; Annex E.3.3's 2023 intrinsic delta touches items 25/26 = EXCEPTION-FILE and EXCEPTION-FILE-N ONLY, never §15.33; the interrogated facility (14.6.13.1.1 last exception status, 7.3.25 TURN, RAISE) is 2002. I then ran the gate myself: --std 85 -> error COBOLNET1502 "FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS was introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002 (15)"; --std 2002/2014/2023 all compile and run identically. Corroboration only.

WHY STILL PARTIAL AND NOT DIVERGES: 15.33.2's own transcribed format (FUNCTION required, no argument list) is implemented correctly at every edition in the window, and wherever the reference binds the value is right. What fails is the 8.4.3.1.2-Format-1 REACH of a function-identifier into three statement-operand slots that reject it outright plus one that silently mis-compiles it — a channel gap common to EVERY function (all four reproduce identically with FUNCTION UPPER-CASE), not a contradiction of THIS format.

subject: LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> DIVERGES. The prior record closed this row on the 8.4.3.2.3 SR2 keyword-omitted form working under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.`. That form is SILENTLY DEFEATABLE, and the defeat produces a WRONG VALUE with no diagnostic. 8.3.2.1 rule 5 (--check OK): 'Intrinsic-function-names may be used as user-defined words and system-names, except for - intrinsic function names LENGTH, RANDOM, SIGN, and SUM; and - intrinsic function names identified in a function-specifier in the REPOSITORY paragraph.' So inside a scope whose REPOSITORY names LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC (by name or by ALL), the word may NOT be a user-defined word - that prohibition is exactly what keeps SR2's keyword-omitted form unambiguous. COBOL.NET never enforces it. `01 LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC PIC S999.` compiles clean under BOTH `FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC` and `FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC INTRINSIC`, and the compiler then resolves the collision with a HAND-WRITTEN PRECEDENCE RULE in place of the standard's prohibition: KeywordOmittedFunction contains `if (ctx.Symbols.TryResolve(name, ctx.ActiveScope, out _)) return null;   // a declared data item wins - never a mis-routed subscript`, and its own doc comment states the policy as 'Data-item-safe: a name that ALSO resolves to a declared data item stays a subscript (a data item wins - zero regression).' That policy is only safe if the illegal declaration is rejected, and it is not. Consequence demonstrated: with `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC INTRINSIC.` and a table named LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC in scope, `MOVE LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(A1) TO R1` - literally 15.58.2's format in its SR2 alternative - yields +7 (the table element) instead of -999, with ZERO diagnostics. ROOT CAUSE: DataBinder#Bind fills RepositoryIntrinsics / RepositoryAllIntrinsic and those sets are consumed ONLY at reference sites in IntrinsicBinder; nothing consults them at DECLARATION time, so 8.3.2.1 r5 is written down nowhere. WHY THE PRIOR RECORD'S CONTROL DOES NOT ATTRIBUTE THIS AWAY: its control was `MOVE ZZQQ-NOPE(A) TO R1`, and ZZQQ-NOPE is not an intrinsic-function-name, so 8.3.2.1 r5 has nothing to say about it - there is no control that makes this generic. SECOND LEG, retained from the prior record and re-run: `LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC(A1)` with NO REPOSITORY at all compiles with zero diagnostics and aborts at RUN TIME with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException - the PB7 shape, invisible to output sampling. SCOPE: the defect is compiler-wide across every intrinsic-function-name, so it is one fix serving many inventory rows; file it once and cross-reference. CONFORMING LEGS, verified this pass and unchanged: two required words, exactly one argument, parentheses required, arity 0 and 2 both COBOLNET1504, `()` also 1504, ref-modification of the numeric result correctly rejected COBOLNET1629 (8.4.3.3.3 SR2), the SR2 form works under BOTH `FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC` and `FUNCTION LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC INTRINSIC` when no data item shadows it, and the name IS correctly available as a user-defined word when NO REPOSITORY function-specifier names it (8.3.2.1 r5's default). editions deliberately EMPTY: the 2023 document does not date 15.58 in Annex E or F, so the window is not spec-derivable from the document under review, and IntrinsicCatalog's own 2002 row is not admissible evidence. subject: MEDIAN function
notes:
REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Two independent grounds.
(1) ⛔ THE VARIABLE-REPETITION HALF OF THE FORMAT IS NOT IMPLEMENTED. `{ argument-1 } …` is precisely what §15.3 means by "When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times" — and §15.3 then defines THREE ranges for the ALL subscript it entitles: a plain OCCURS count, "If the ALL subscript is associated with a data item described with an OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause, the range of values is determined by the object of the OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause" (cite.py --check 15.3 => OK §15.3 14)), and "If the subscript ALL is specified for a dynamic-capacity table, the range of values of the subscript is from 1 to the current capacity of the table." Only the FIRST works. `TryExpandAll` emits `new BoundOperandError($"table(ALL) over OCCURS DEPENDING table '{name}' …")` at its `if (levels[i].OccursSpec?.Depending is not null)` arm — the program COMPILES CLEAN and dies at RUN time. That is the PB7 shape exactly: invisible to output sampling because compilation succeeds. And the token DYNAMIC appears in NO .g4 file in src/Cobol.Net.Compiler, so the dynamic-capacity range can never be produced at all. So for the one case the `…` exists to express — an argument count that is genuinely variable — MEDIAN produces no value.
(2) The adjudication's OWN FMT evidence file (med_all_a.cob) is the file that throws; its fixed-OCCURS half was cited under FMT and its ODO half attributed only to the RV rows. One rule, two halves, one verified => PARTIAL.

subject: MIDRANGE function
notes: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The adjudicator verified the SYNTAX SHAPE and stopped there. The format's load-bearing element is `{ argument-1 } …` — the VARIABLE-REPETITION argument list — and §15.3 r14 defines, normatively, the form that list may take: "When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times, a table may be referenced by specifying the data-name and any qualifiers that identify the table, followed immediately by subscripting where one or more of the subscripts is the word ALL", with TWO further sentences the compiler does not implement — "If the subscript ALL is specified for a dynamic-capacity table, the range of values of the subscript is from 1 to the current capacity of the table" and "If the ALL subscript is associated with a data item described with an OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause, the range of values is determined by the object of the OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause." TWO GAPS, BOTH PB7-SHAPED — the program COMPILES CLEAN with no diagnostic and dies at RUN TIME, which is precisely why probing a fixed-OCCURS table(ALL) and reading its correct answer could not see them. (1) table(ALL) over an OCCURS DEPENDING ON table: IntrinsicBinder.TryExpandAll tests `levels[i].OccursSpec?.Depending is not null` and emits a BoundOperandError BY DESIGN (its own doc-comment says "a runtime quantity this bind-time expansion cannot produce; staged loud by name"), which lands as NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at run time. (2) table(ALL) over an OCCURS DYNAMIC (dynamic-capacity) table: TryExpandAll builds its OCCURS-level chain from `n.Occurs is not null`, which is null for a dynamic-capacity item, so levels.Count (0) != innerSegs.Count (1) and it falls into the WRONG arm — the diagnostic reads "table(ALL) subscript count for 'T'", which misdescribes the defect and would send the next reader after a subscript-arity bug that is not there. THE VERDICT IS PARTIAL, NOT CONFORMS-WITH-A-NOTE: a run-time NotImplemented on legal source is unimplemented feature, i.e. debt under CLAUDE.md rule 3, and it is unimplemented for MIDRANGE specifically because MIDRANGE is one of the variadic functions §15.3 r14 exists to serve. WHAT IS GENUINELY RIGHT (re-verified, so the fix is not over-scoped): the arity screen rejects the zero-argument and empty-parenthesis forms the format forbids; a single argument, n arguments, negatives, fractions, identifiers, a nested MIDRANGE call, a fixed-OCCURS table(ALL), and the §8.4.3.2 SR2 keyword-omitted comma-separated form under REPOSITORY FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC all bind correctly — including the keyword-omitted form COMBINED with table(ALL), which I probed specifically because that is where PB7 lived. The transcribed diagram is corroborated by the §15.6 summary row `| MIDRANGE | Num1 … | Num |` (one-or-more numeric in, numeric out); I did not re-render the PDF and record the adjudicator's render as corroboration, not as my own evidence. EDITIONS: the ODO leg was probed at --std 85 and --std 2023 and fails identically at both; I do not state an edition window for the dynamic-capacity leg because I did not derive OCCURS DYNAMIC's introduction from the spec. EVIDENCE: cite.py --check 15.62.2 "<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>MIDRANGE</u> ( { argument-1 } … )" -> OK §15.62.2 (General format). cite.py --check 15.3 "If the ALL subscript is associated with a data item described with an OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause, the range of values is determined by the object of the OCCURS DEPENDING ON clause." -> OK §15.3 14) (Arguments). REFUTER PROBE 1, E:/Temp/rfmid/rfmidodo.cob (PROGRAM-ID RFMIDODO): `05 T PIC S9(4)V99 OCCURS 1 TO 5 TIMES DEPENDING ON N` with N=3, T(1..3) = 1.00/5.00/9.00, `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MIDRANGE(T(ALL))`. COMPILED CLEAN at --std 2023 (no diagnostic at all) and at --std 85; at RUN TIME both threw `CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... table(ALL) over OCCURS DEPENDING table 'T' (current-count expansion, 15.3)`. Correct answer is (1.00+9.00)/2 = 5.0000. REFUTER PROBE 2, E:/Temp/rfmid/rfmiddy2.cob (PROGRAM-ID RFMIDDY2): `05 T PIC S9(4)V99 OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY IN CAP`, same three values. COMPILED CLEAN at --std 2023; the run printed CAP=0000000003 (so the capacity register is correct and populated) and then threw `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... table(ALL) subscript count for 'T'`. ATTRIBUTABLE CONTROLS, both compiled and ran: E:/Temp/rfmid/rfmidfix.cob (fixed `OCCURS 3 TIMES`, same values) printed FIX=000005000{ = 5.0000 — correct; E:/Temp/rfmid/rfmidrep.cob under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` printed REPALL=000005000{ for the keyword-omitted `MIDRANGE(T(ALL))` and REPLIT=000005500{ for `MIDRANGE(1, 2, 10)` — so the keyword-omitted path is NOT the defect and the fixed-OCCURS ALL expansion is correct. E:/Temp/rfmid/rfmidctl.cob printed CTL=000005750{ for MIDRANGE(1.5 2.5 10.0) = 5.7500. Source read: IntrinsicBinder.cs#TryExpandAll — the ODO arm and the `levels.Count != innerSegs.Count` arm.

subject: MIN function
notes: REFUTER RE-EXAMINED AND SUSTAINED — the one row that survived attack, and the format DIAGRAM was rendered from the PDF rather than trusted from the transcription (CLAUDE.md rule 1: a general format is a load-bearing diagram). Printed folio 888 / PDF page 918 renders as `FUNCTION MIN ( { argument-1 } … )` with FUNCTION and MIN both UNDERLINED and nothing bracketed — exactly what specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.63.2 carries, so the transcription is faithful and no falsely-restrictive OCR residue is in play here. The grammar rule `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` is a deliberate SUPERSET — the parenthesised group is optional there and the per-function arity is the binder's job. For MIN the catalog row is Variadic with a minimum of 1 (`Add(new("MIN", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "p", "MinScaled", ...))`) and the binder enforces it, so the composite behaviour matches the printed format: FUNCTION required, MIN required, the parenthesised list required, at least one argument required, repetition unbounded. The repeat-brace `…` also picks up §15.3's ALL-subscript expansion, which works. ⚠ RESIDUE (unchanged, and it is a corpus gap not a conformance defect): no spec-derived test pins the two REJECTION shapes (bare `FUNCTION MIN`, empty `FUNCTION MIN()`) — test-ref is deliberately left EMPTY rather than closed on the differential. ⚠ SCOPE NOTE the refuter adds: §15.63.1's TYPE TABLE (Index ⇒ Index, All arguments integer ⇒ Integer) is visible on the same rendered page and is NOT covered by any rule in this batch — the catalog hardcodes IntrinsicType.Numeric and the binder only ever re-derives Alphanumeric/National. Whether the Integer and Index rows of that table are honoured is an UNADJUDICATED row, and it should be added to the inventory rather than assumed closed by this FMT verdict. EVIDENCE: PDF page rendered: `python scripts/spec/clause_page.py 15.63.1 15.63.2 15.63.3` → PDF page 918 / printed folio 888; `python scripts/render-spec-page.py 918` → E:/Temp/spec_p918.png, read and compared against the transcription. FUNCTION MIN INTRINSIC.` works. subject: MOD function
notes:
REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL, and the test-ref and editions are both withdrawn. THREE separate refutations.
(1) THE CITED TEST DOES NOT TEST THIS RULE. `IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.Mod_SignTable_PinnedToSpec` is a genuine spec-derived fixture (read it: `AssertSpec` runs COBOL.NET ONLY and asserts a literal — it is not the `AssertSameAsLegacy`/`DifferentialGolden` helper in the same file), but what it pins is the four §15.64.4 NOTE rows, i.e. the RETURNED VALUE. It contains no arity arm, no separator arm and no rejection arm, so it cannot close a GENERAL FORMAT row. The adjudication's own note conceded the point — 'the negative arity arms are probe-verified only, not pinned by a fixture' — and then listed the test anyway. test-ref cleared.
(2) THE ALL-SUBSCRIPT FORM IS ACCEPTED, AND MOD'S FORMAT DOES NOT PERMIT IT. §15.3 rule 14 (--check verified) grants the device conditionally: 'When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a VARIABLE number of times, a table may be referenced by specifying the data-name ... followed immediately by subscripting where one or more of the subscripts is the word ALL.' §15.64.2's format is `FUNCTION MOD ( argument-1 argument-2 )` — fixed at two, no ellipsis — so ALL is not available to MOD at all. `IntrinsicBinder.TryExpandAll` runs for EVERY argument of EVERY function and never consults the catalog's arity kind; its own doc comment states the correct rule ('when a VARIADIC function references a table with the ALL subscript') and the code does not implement it. The only thing standing between the expansion and acceptance is the arity screen counting the EXPANSION, so the restriction is enforced ONLY when the element count happens to miss 2 — an accident of the OCCURS count, not a rule. This is the shape memory-flagged as `model_the_rule_shape_not_one_case`: a screen that measures the wrong quantity.
(3) EDITIONS WERE NOT MEASURED AND NOT SPEC-DERIVED. The prior record asserted '85,2002,2014,2023' while every FMT probe in its own evidence ran at `--std 2023` alone. The window is also not derivable from the standard here: §15.64 carries no edition qualifier, Annex E (substantive changes) does not mention MOD, and `docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md` has no MOD row — so the only remaining source is the trailing `85` in IntrinsicCatalog's own MOD row, which is the forbidden derivation (deriving the answer from the code under review). Cleared rather than guessed.
WHAT SURVIVES AND IS RE-VERIFIED: the printed diagram (rendered PDF page 919) is `FUNCTION MOD ( argument-1 argument-2 )` with FUNCTION and MOD underlined, no optional element, no ellipsis — the OCR transcription is faithful; the generic keyword-led `functionCall` rule plus the catalog row `IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2` rejects 0/1/3 arguments with COBOLNET1504; the §8.4.3.2.3 keyword-omitted (REPOSITORY ... INTRINSIC) form resolves; and reference modification of the result is correctly refused (a boundary the prior pass did not probe). EVIDENCE: Re-probed with the already-built compiler, `--std 2023`, unique PROGRAM-ID per file, all under E:/Temp/modref/.
 · CONTROL MODRF01 — `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MOD(A B)` -> +000000000000000001 and `DISPLAY ... FUNCTION MOD(A B)` -> 1. The harness is sound, so every rejection below is attributable.
 · MODRF08 — `FUNCTION MOD()` -> `error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION MOD takes 2 argument(s); 0 given (ISO 15.3)`.
 · MODRF06 — `MOVE FUNCTION MOD(11 5)(1:1) TO T` -> `error COBOLNET1629: 'FUNCTION MOD' is not an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function, so its result cannot be reference-modified (ISO 8.4.3.3.3 SR2)`. Correct; the format admits no reference modifier.
 · MODRF07 — `05 E PIC S9(4) OCCURS 3 TIMES.` then `FUNCTION MOD(E(ALL) B)` -> `COBOLNET1504: ... 2 argument(s); 4 GIVEN`. Note the count: the ALL expansion has already happened and the arity screen is counting its OUTPUT. The rejection is incidental.
 · MODRF09 — THE REFUTATION. The identical program with `OCCURS 1 TIMES` COMPILES CLEAN (exit 0) and prints `ALL1 = +0001`. So `FUNCTION MOD(E(ALL) B)` is accepted whenever the expansion lands on 2, and §15.3 rule 14's restriction is nowhere enforced.
Source read, not sampled: `IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore` calls `TryExpandAll(a, args)` inside the per-argument loop with no arity/variadicity guard; `IntrinsicCatalog.Build` row is `Add(new("MOD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2, "ii", "ModScaled", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 85))`.
Citations validated: `python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 15.3 "When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times, a table may be referenced by specifying the data-name and any qualifiers that identify the table, followed immediately by subscripting where one or more of the subscripts is the word ALL."` -> OK §15.3 14); `--check 15.64.1 "The MOD function returns an integer value that is argument-1 modulo argument-2."` -> OK §15.64.1. Annex E scanned for MOD: absent (so 2014->2023 is unchanged; nothing establishes 85/2002 from the spec text).

subject: MODULE-NAME function
notes: Verdict SUSTAINED, on re-derived grounds rather than the original ones. I read BindModuleName rather than sampling: `kind` starts at -1 and the loop errors on the FIRST non-keyword or on any argument once `kind >= 0`, then errors again if the loop saw none — so both arity bounds are structural. Two attack lines the adjudicator did not run, both of which the format rule actually reaches, come out clean. (1) THE FUNCTION-KEYWORD-OMITTED FORM. §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 and §12.3.8 SR13 make `FUNCTION` omissible for any intrinsic the REPOSITORY declares, and §15.65 carries no rule requiring the keyword — this is the exact shape of the landed PB7/PB9 defects, and MODULE-NAME is not covered by either (it is not a §8.9 reserved name and it is not zero-argument, so it takes the D2 dataReference re-route in KeywordOmittedFunction). It works, including for the reserved-word argument NESTED, under both `FUNCTION MODULE-NAME INTRINSIC` and `FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC`. (2) RESULT REFERENCE MODIFICATION (§8.4.3.3.3 SR2) and lower-case keywords both work. Residual, recorded but not verdict-changing: NEITHER cited test exercises the rule's own content — the arity bound (zero / two / non-keyword arguments) and the NESTED and STACK keywords are pinned by no test at all, so the structural enforcement I verified by hand is undefended against drift. Editions re-derived from the SPEC, not the catalog row: Annex E.3.3 item 28 (checked) plus Annex F.13 item 13, which lists MODULE-NAME among the intrinsic names ADDED by this edition. EVIDENCE: New probes, already-built cobol.exe, --std 2023, control MNREFCTL1 succeeded ('CTL-CUR=[MNREFCTL1]'). Keyword-omitted: E:/Temp/mnref/omit.cob (REPOSITORY. FUNCTION MODULE-NAME INTRINSIC) -> 'OMIT-CUR=[MNREFOMIT1]' / 'OMIT-TOP=[MNREFOMIT1]'; omitall.cob (FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC) -> 'ALL-CUR=[MNREFALL1]'; omitnest.cob -> 'IN-NST=[MNROMNS1-IN]' 'IN-ACT=[MNROMNS1]' 'IN-STK=[MNROMNS1; ]' (the reserved word NESTED survives the ReparseArgs round trip). Ref-mod: refmod.cob 'FUNCTION MODULE-NAME(CURRENT) (1:3)' -> 'RM=[MNR]'. Case: lower.cob '(current)' -> 'LOW=[MNREFLOW1]' (KeywordWordOf upper-cases). Rejections re-run: emptyp.cob '()' -> COBOLNET1504 'requires one keyword argument'; figarg.cob '(SPACE)' and badarg.cob '(TE(1))' -> COBOLNET1504 "...not 'SPACE'" / "...not 'TE(1)'". Edition sweep EXTENDED past the adjudicator's single 2014 point: ctl.cob at --std 85 and --std 2002 both -> COBOLNET1502 'introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2023'. Citations checked: `cite.py --check E.3.3 "The MODULE-NAME intrinsic function has been added to provide information about the modules in the hierarchy of the running application."` -> OK item 28; §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 and §12.3.8 SR13 read directly from specs/ISO_COBOL.md; Annex F.13 item 13 lists MODULE-NAME.

subject: NUMVAL function
notes: CONFORMS SUSTAINED -- and, unlike the adjudication, it now survives the boundaries it had merely asserted. The general format has no optional or repeated element: FUNCTION and NUMVAL are both underlined (required) and there is exactly one parenthesized argument; the catalog row declares `IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1` and BindIntrinsicCore enforces it with COBOLNET1504 in BOTH directions. Three additional attacks were run and all failed to overturn it. (i) PB7's pattern -- a form that compiles and dies at run time: the FUNCTION-keyword-omitted form under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` compiles AND RUNS correctly, so the omission license does not strand NUMVAL. (ii) Over-reservation: an intrinsic-function-name is not a reserved word unless the REPOSITORY declares it, and `01 NUMVAL PIC X(6)` is accepted alongside `FUNCTION NUMVAL(NUMVAL)` -- the lexer token does not leak into the user-defined-word space, so no legal source is rejected. subject: NUMVAL-C function
notes: REFUTED: PARTIAL -> DIVERGES, and the `editions` field emptied. (A) ORDER. The prior record found ONE order violation (ANYCASE accepted between argument-1 and argument-2) and held the row at PARTIAL. BindNumvalCFamily's `foreach (var a in argCtxs)` is positionally blind in BOTH directions and has no once-only guard, and two further accepted shapes are non-conforming under ANY reading of the general-format diagram — including a lossy OCR of it — so settling them needs no PDF render: (a) ANYCASE placed BEFORE argument-1, `FUNCTION NUMVAL-C(ANYCASE WS-A "USD")`, where argument-1 sits immediately after the open parenthesis in the format and §15.68.3 r1 names it the first argument, so nothing admits a keyword ahead of it; (b) ANYCASE specified TWICE, `FUNCTION NUMVAL-C(WS-A "USD" ANYCASE ANYCASE)`, where the format carries exactly one [ANYCASE]. Both compile clean and evaluate as though ANYCASE sat in its legal place. A format that silently accepts three distinct shapes it does not describe is a divergence, not a partial implementation. Only the ANYCASE-vs-argument-2 ORDERING is genuinely diagram-dependent, and the verdict no longer rests on it. (B) EDITIONS EMPTIED. The prior record's window was inferred from Annex E.3.3 item 1's 'has been clarified to be consistent with the rest of the standard'. Annex E is INFORMATIVE and E.1 scopes it to 'the substantive changes between the previous COBOL standard and this Working Draft' — 'clarified' fixes no introduction edition and says nothing whatever about 1985 or 2002. Per the edition discipline an unproven window is left EMPTY rather than half-asserted; the observation is retained here. The gate itself remains unverified and unbuilt: neither ANYCASE nor the LOCALE phrase has an edition predicate of its own, so ANYCASE compiles at --std 85 and --std 2002 on the strength of a catalog row (IntroducedIn 85) that is the code under review and cannot be its own evidence. POSITIVE, newly probed: a reference-modified argument-1 binds and values correctly, and arity is genuinely enforced (COBOLNET1504). subject: SIN function
notes: Citation validated: cite.py --check 15.82.2 '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>SIN</u> ( argument-1 )' -> OK. The format parses through functionCall's first alternative (FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? ...), SIN arriving as IDENTIFIER through functionName and resolving against the catalog row ("SIN", Numeric, Fixed, 1, 1, ..., IntrinsicBind.Runtime, Float:true). The diagram's required elements are all enforced: FUNCTION and SIN are required by the grammar alternative (SIN is not in reservedIntrinsicArgFn, so no keyword-omitted grammar form exists for it; the REPOSITORY omission is S8.4.3.2.3 SR2's separate allowance, handled by binder re-route); the parenthesized single argument is required at bind - the paren group is grammatically optional for zero-argument functions, and a bare FUNCTION SIN is rejected by the Fixed 1,1 arity check (COBOLNET1504), as is any second argument. The FNARG_LPAREN retyping implements S8.4.3.2.3 SR6 (the '(' after the name is always the argument list). Editions derived independently of the catalog row: SIN entered with the 1989 Intrinsic Function amendment to COBOL-85 (it is exercised by the NIST CCVS-85 suite, IF135A) and appears in NO later-edition delta row of docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md (the 2023 seven-function delta, rows 65-73, does not include it), so it is present at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023.
